💡 Key Takeaways

In a recent development, (ANSA) - MILANO, 18 NOV - "Adriano Galliani lo conosco da 45 anni, lo stimo, è una persona capacissima. Ma io appoggio Malagò perché secondo me è giusto avere una coerenza di comportamento: lo abbiamo appoggiato a maggio, lo abbiamo votato a giugno, sostenuto a luglio, lui abbastanza in solitaria ha scelto Mancini che ha dato segnali positivi. Poi è partito il tema del tesseramento, il commissariamento e la nuova elezione, ma tutto ciò non è di quello di cui ha bisogno il calcio". Lo dice il presidente del Torino, Urbano Cairo, parlando delle elezioni della Figc che vedono in lizza Adriano Galliani e Giovanni Malagò. "Facciamo queste elezioni - aggiunge Cairo a margine dell'evento Rcs Sport Industry Talk -, manca meno di un mese, poi dobbiamo ripartire velocemente.

I temi sul tavolo sono tanti, chi vincerà avrà 100 giorni davanti per poter dare una spinta e un impulso nuovo. È un peccato, gli ultimi due mesi sono stati praticamente buttati. Fortunatamente la Nazionale ha dato qualche buon segnale quindi ripartiamo da quello e cerchiamo di fare cose buone, il calcio italiano ha un potenziale elevatissimo". (ANSA).

Industry observers note that ivana Andres, difensore dell'Inter Women, ha presentato ai microfoni di Inter TV la sfida di Women's Champions League contro il Real Madrid, sua ex squadra: "Servirà rimanere molto concentrate ed essere in partita per fare il nostro gioco, questo è quello che ci chiede anche l'allenatore. Dobbiamo avere massima concentrazione per tutta la partita e mantenere l'ambizione di conquistare questi tre punti.

Tornare qui per me è speciale, è stata casa mia per quattro anni: sarà una partita emozionante per me, ho tanti bei ricordi perché qui sono cresciuta come giocatrice e come donna. La difesa è il miglior attacco: se non si prendono gol si è sempre sicuri di non perdere le partite. Difendere e attaccare bene però è una responsabilità che riguarda tutta la squadra e che tutte abbiamo. A livello personale io cerco sempre di dare il massimo per le mie compagne e per la squadra".

Il tecnico del Catanzaro Michele Mignani in vista della sfida contro il Palermo nel prossimo turno potrebbe dover far a meno di Simone Pafundi, nuovamente alle prese con un problema muscolare dopo quello che lo colpì a inizio stagione facendogli saltare le prime tre gare di campionato.

Il fantasista classe 2006 infatti soffre per un fastidio al polpaccio che lo stando condizionando in questi giorni e che potrebbe fargli saltare la sfida contro il rosanero. Una situazione da monitorare con attenzione in attesa delle valutazioni che farà lo staff medico, che lo sta monitorando giornalmente, da qui al fine settimana. Una decisione sulla sua disponibilità, come riporta La Gazzetta dello Sport, arriverà probabilmente solo a ridosso della sfida contro i siciliani, ma al momento la presenza di Pafundi appare molto in dubbio.

In a recent development, un gesto di solidarietà che può fare la differenza. Sabato 21 novembre, dalle 9 alle 13, il Center Union di Aversa, in Viale Kennedy 35, ospiterà “Dona, fai la differenza”, iniziativa promossa da Union Gas e Luce in collaborazione con la Casa del Donatore di Aversa per sensibilizzare sull’importanza della donazione del sangue.

According to recent reports, all’evento parteciperà anche Patrizio Oliva, campione olimpico di pugilato e testimonial di Union, che incontrerà i partecipanti e sosterrà la campagna di sensibilizzazione. «Non serve essere campioni per fare un gesto da campioni», è il messaggio lanciato dall’ex pugile. L’iniziativa si inserisce nell’impegno di Union a favore del territorio e della responsabilità sociale, con l’obiettivo di coinvolgere cittadini, associazioni e realtà locali nella promozione della cultura della donazione. «L’energia più bella è quella che condividiamo», il messaggio che accompagna l’evento.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The noise started in a corner of the South Stand, early in the second half. It was muffled at first, but as the ball popped from one white shirt to another, it became louder and louder, sweeping around the stadium: here was the soundtrack for a humiliation.

“Olé! Olé! Olé!” they roared and why not? Leeds were ripping Newcastle to pieces, knocking passes around them as if they were training-ground mannequins. Football has become a sport that leaves people increasingly vexed, but this was a night when – for the locals, at least – it was almost a throwback.

There was energy and ferocious tackling, a No 9 soaring like centre-forwards used to in the not-too-distant past and lots of goals as Leeds cut loose and abruptly ended whatever honeymoon Matthias Jaissle had been experiencing in charge of Newcastle.

It has been revealed that “I suppose in football you can always find something to moan about,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds manager, mentioned. “But this was a top-class performance.”.

Industry observers note that it has felt suspiciously like Newcastle’s start has been like an overstuffed plastic shopping bag, the handles straining to the point of snapping. Eventually they fell asunder. Leeds ran all over them and were too smart, slick and hungry, not to mention ruthless. No wonder Jaissle had nowhere to go.

Industry observers note that the home fans were adamant this was one of the best nights Leeds have experienced under Farke and if they were prepared to say as much, you had an obligation to listen. Forget how wretched Newcastle were, Leeds had produced a performance to enable imaginations to run wild.

Centre to it all was Ao Tanaka, with his desire to keep Leeds playing forward, but it felt wrong to talk about one man when you had the unstoppable Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who would be substituted to a standing ovation, and the ubiquitous James Justin, among others.

"He just cannot stop scoring at Elland Road" 🔥Dominic Calvert-Lewin makes it 2-0 to Leeds! pic.twitter.com/Pv1TEpc5Qj.

The foundations are being put in around the stadium for a cavernous latest West Stand, and Farke’s remit is to ensure that Leeds will be firmly established in the Premier League by the time it is completed in the summer of 2028.

To be fair to Farke, he has laid a sturdy base for this team to thrive and it felt before kick-off that this was going to be a major evening for Leeds, who had made a quietly encouraging start to the campaign and had negotiated three challenging away trips without defeat.

Big? It turned out to be spectacular. The first half was so one-sided that a boxing referee would not have allowed Newcastle to come out for the second, such was the pummelling they received; wave after wave of white-shirted raids left the visitors black and blue.

Aside from one little rick inside the opening 10 minutes, when James Trafford dithered and presented Yoane Wissa with a chance to mug him, Leeds were every bit as sensational as Newcastle were shocking, seizing on the opportunity to go on a rampage.

Industry observers note that leeds would have been in front after 11 minutes but Ethan Ampadu’s fierce drive battered into Calvert-Lewin’s legs and bounced away. Normally in such circumstances, players will wave an arm to berate their bad luck, but Ampadu, celebrating his 26th birthday, smiled: he, like everyone else, sensed what was coming.

Jayden Bogle, Justin and Nico Elvedi all had opportunities to open the scoring earlier, but eventually, they found the weak spot. Newcastle, who had lost the influential Nico González to a potential concussion, had replaced him with Sean Steur and what an influence he would have on matters.

On the half hour, Steur was a fraction too late getting out to close down Tanaka, whose shot ricocheted off him and to Lewis Miley, before looping away from Lukas Hornicek and dropping into the corner of the net in dam-busting fashion.

Ao Tanaka's deflected effort puts Leeds ahead! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/cYXVi3LOAO.

According to recent reports, leeds were running even quicker by this point, pressing as if their lives depended on it and making tackles that were lustily acclaimed in the stands. Steur completely short-circuited in the bedlam and a ridiculous pass on the edge of his area was pounced upon by Bogle.

Out went a ball to Justin, whose cross was whipped into the penalty area, where Calvert-Lewin had climbed to get his head to it, though replays indicated his effort glanced off Bogle’s head – determining the true scorer will make for an interesting conversation.

Calvert-Lewin, at least, got the reward his efforts deserved on the cusp of half-time, spinning away from Miley and chopping inside Sven Botman before delivering the kind of finish that should make Thomas Tuchel take note when selecting his next England squad this week.

"They are relentless!"Dominic Calvert-Lewin caps off a dominant first-half from Leeds 💪 pic.twitter.com/S6kQykOMW9.

The gloss, after those “olés”, was applied in the 59th minute when Noah Okafor put a realistic hue on the score, ramming in a finish in front of the Kop and leaving Newcastle open to the crudest mocking for the amount of money they have spent to resemble such a disorganised rabble.

A wonderful strike with equally brilliant celebrations from Noah Okafor! 🕺 pic.twitter.com/Ce1ueKtH4x.

Bazoumana Touré, at least, scored a consolation goal, but Jaissle barely flickered as it went in and the emotion belonged to Farke, who thundered on to the pitch at the final whistle and sought out his captain, Ampadu, who had erred in allowing Newcastle’s substitute to profit.

Sources indicate that “That was an unnecessary goal to concede and I so wanted us to keep a clean sheet,” Farke sighed. “We deserved a clean sheet and I couldn’t help myself. I had to tell him because I am sometimes a perfectionist. We must try to stay humble, but we can be an outstanding team.”.

And this, for certain, was an outstanding night.

[It was brutal out there?] That’s football. That’s the Premier League. It was clear from the start and I have remarked it many times. We will have ups and downs and challenges all the way. Tonight we faced that challenge. It’s tough and difficult to digest. But there is a chance to learn out of that and there’s a long time until our next match at home and that is good.

Industry observers note that it’s clear with our young squad that there will be ups and downs and you have to bring the fundamentals on the pitch against such a physical team. Leeds are so intense, we couldn’t match that physicality. There are other aspects of course but I don’t want to make excuses. We want to learn out of it and be better.

[Were you overwhelmed as a team?] No. If you don’t bring that physicality on the pitch, you struggle.

Exactly this [message to the players]. Bring your fundamentals and we build on it. [Can you bounce back from this in your next game?] Of course. [Is your confidence hit?] No.

For each manager it would be a nightmare after such a game to concede so late and not have the well-deserved clean sheet. Of course I was not happy about the situation. Doesn’t take anything away from my boys who were magnificent. Terrific start with eight points but there’s never a perfect performance. There’s always something to moan about. At very rare points [in the season] I have to criticise [for conceding].

Energy, quality, good structure, in an out of possession, which is complicated against Newcastle, In pressing them you always have to be aware of their unbelievable pace and strength in counter-attacks. We found this balance today and in the first half particularly we were dominant.

It has been revealed that we have a good fitness level now. Need to find the right triggers to press. It’s a lot of well-structured work on the training ground. We had more chances to score tonight but overall I am very happy with our performance.

Recent findings suggest that [Calvert-Lewin being praised] It is well deserved. He is in outstanding shape and plays with lots of confidence. I expect him to lead the group with some other players. His work-rate is never in doubt and to me he is one of the best strikers in the league.

The ref told me at half-time that they’ve taken it off me. I didn’t know he [Bogle] was there to be fair. I just got up and went ‘Bang!’ It is what it is. I’ll take the assist!

In a recent development, I didn’t know anything about it [being given credit for the second goal]. I remarked to the ref, I don’t fancy telling him [Calvert-Lewin]. To be fair he’s still raging. He’s raging with the goal but happy with the result.

Recent findings suggest that it’s about having an understanding with the players around you. With Dom up there, you know he’s going to win everything so you have to get the runners around him.

It has been revealed that it’s about the rotation like today. When James Justin goes wider there’s space inside. Dom occupies two centre-backs so there’s always pockets.

Regardless of the scoreline it was a tough game physically. They’re a very good side. We take it game by game, not to get carried away. Everyone’s ambitious in their own way but we have to take it game by game.

A proper stuffing for Newcastle as Leeds continue to impress and climb up to third.

James pounces on a loose ball, dribbles infield from the right. No one bothers to close him down so he eventually has a shot, blazing over with his left from 20 yards.

Newcastle are passive, they look disorganised in midfield and weak at the back. Oh and they barely apply pressure let alone attack dangerously.

What better way to play through a press than to bypass the midfield completely? The hope is it will also cause the centre-backs problems, get them facing their own goal under pressure from one of Newcastle’s rapid forward players in a foot race.

It almost worked a couple of times in the first half but it should be pointed out that the best direct/long ball teams of the past tended to have a striker who was dominant in the air. Newcastle do not presently have one which does limit their threat from flick ons.

The reason it is a problem is because we have become conditioned to thinking every time a ball touches someone on the arm in the area, a penalty should be awarded. It is preposterous that faceless beaks have distorted the game so much.

Leeds are in their home kit of white with yellow and blue pinstripe hoops, Newcastle in their navy away kit.

Anthony [Elanga] is injured. Unfortunately we have to investigate further how long he will be out but obviously we miss him. We wish him to come back as rapidly as possible. It could be [a long-term injury] but he will get another MRI next week and then we’ll see.

Recent findings suggest that lewis Hall is the perfect player profile for how we play. he is a young lad still and we are very excited [that he has signed a fresh contract].

The start was not easy. We didn’t have lots of time to prepare for pre-season and that’s one reason we are happy and satisfied with the start. But there is potential and we will work hard on the margins we want to improve.

There will be a lot of excitement surrounding Mathias Fernandez-Pardo’s first start for Newcastle United following his deadline day move from Lille but also keep an eye on Jacob Murphy on the right wing.

Fernandez-Pardo starts with a clean slate at Newcastle, Murphy has a lot of baggage and he has been a popular online target for criticism over the last year or so.

Indeed, some sections of the fanbase were stunned Newcastle rejected a £15m offer from Nottingham Forest on deadline day for a player who has entered the final 12 months of his contract.

Murphy has his limitations, sure and he can be infuriating sometimes when he gives the ball away cheaply, but there is a reason Matthias Jaissle was adamant he could not be sold.

Part of that is due to the fact he does not have another specialist right winger behind Anthony Elanga who misses the Leeds game through injury.

Sources indicate that but Murphy is also valued for his experience and his training ground presence. He has been at the club a long time, working under Rafa Benítez, Steve Bruce and Eddie Howe and is a boyhood Newcastle fan.

Sources indicate that jaissle was not willing to lose that from his dressing room. Ultimately, though, Murphy has to perform on the pitch to justify the faith shown in him.

There are not many other options to fill that position while Elanga is missing. Harvey Barnes does not like playing on the right, Amar Dedic is a full back and so is Tino Livramento.

Industry observers note that this is an opportunity for Murphy to silence his detractors and prove the faith Jaissle has put in him is not misplaced. At the age of 31, he knows he is not the most popular or appreciated player at the club but he has never shirked or complained about that.

It has been revealed that he formed a potent partnership with Alexander Isak when he was leading the line for Newcastle. Can he do the same with the fresh boy Fernandez-Pardo?

It has been revealed that mind you I remember his visit to Elland Road in 1982-83. Not for the faint hearted. In fact it was a disgrace when he was hit by a coin. And yet he was always gracious about Leeds and particularly fond of Don Revie. He was one of very few football people without a strong Leeds United connection who went to his funeral in 1989.

Apparently he was injured in training, the nature of the injury is unspecified.

According to recent reports, newcastle have made a very good start particularly in their transitional moments on the counter-attack. We have to be switched on today to get the next points.

After many years of suffering our supporters deserve it [high expectations]. It’s good but we are far away from not being humble. Our feet are on the ground. We know the second year is always difficult. We have made a good start and it is always important to ride the momentum as long as possible.

Eddie Howe has left a legacy and the culture he created is still around. Matthias has to work with it. They are unbeaten. they are very dangerous with many pacy players up front. It’s important not to lose the ball too easily and always be switched on against Newcastle.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of Leeds United vs Newcastle United, the last Premier League match of the fourth round of fixtures for the 2026-27 season. Both clubs have made unbeaten starts with one win and two draws each and a win today for wither would send them up to fourth. The two sides met at Elland Road in the third match of last season which ended in a 0-0 draw but the return fixture at St James’ Park was one of the games of the season, a ding-dong match that Leeds led 0-1, 1-2 and 2-3, the latter until the 91st minute and yet still lost 4-3.

Recent findings suggest that the architect of that victory for Newcastle was the Leeds’ fans’ incubus, a player commonly known around Elland Road as ‘Harvey F------- Barnes’. His two goals that night were his sixth and seventh against Leeds in eight matches for Leicester and the Toon. Back in the last century and at the turn of this one, Alan Shearer scored 21 league goals in 23 games against Leeds for Blackburn Rovers and Newcastle, it can feel like one bogeyman passing the baton to another.

Newcastle’s sound form with their new model team this season has been based on searing pace and their ability on the counter whether with runners, in the case of Anthony Elanga, or with long diagonals against Tottenham that ripped a hole in the left side of their defence. Leeds rallied from being overrun by Brentford at half-time in their last home game to switch from three at the back to four and wrest back the initiative and while they reverted for the Brighton draw, in both games it was the introduction of Ao Tanaka in midfield that gave them control.

According to recent reports, it is genuinely hard to decide whether the 6-3 defeat by Chelsea in the Carabao Cup from being 2-0 up at Stamford Bridge is significant to Leeds league form. One simplistic way of looking at it would be to say Leeds reserves were better than Chelsea’s reserves in the first half and Chelsea’s first-team were better than Leeds reserves and their shaky, debutant keeper in the second. But any similar defensive frailties tonight and there will be jitters over the next week before the international break. Newcastle, by contrast, toiled in their 1-0 victory over Millwall but the result glosses over a lack of incision for long spells of it.

Joe Rodon is out for Leeds for at least another month while Newcastle have changed to withholding information about their treatment room under Matthias Jaissle who indicates that it should be ‘confidential’. We do know that Joelinton, William Osula and Dan Burn are likely to still be out given the nature of their injuries but Amar Dedic, who came off at half-time at the New Den with a thigh or hamstring problem, may be back.

RedBird e Gerry Cardinale, per la prima volta, hanno immesso 50 milioni di euro per la gestione dell'area sportiva del Milan. È una notizia di un mese fa, ma fa la differenza rispetto a quanto successo nel recente passato. Perché i rossoneri hanno percorso una strada verso la sostenibilità che ha portato ad avere tre bilanci in utile, mentre l'ultimo è stato un rosso di 24 milioni. Non troppi considerando che non c'era la Champions League che, a certi livelli, fa la differenza. Dopo le spese di quest'estate è chiaro che bisogna alzare l'asticella.

Il Milan in estate ha speso moltissimo sul mercato per finanziare gli acquisti, in particolare, di Gonçalo Ramos e di Diego Moreira Jr, più Mario Gila. Più di 160 milioni di euro controbilanciati da 87 in entrata. È anche vero che questi 160 milioni vanno divisi su quattro o cinque anni, portando l'investimento annuale a circa 38 a stagione. Anche qui, ce ne sono altri da ammortare, ma a parte De Winter e Chukwueze - un pochino Pulisic - gli altri sono praticamente quasi tutti ammortati, quindi pesano a bilancio poco. Un rischio calcolato quindi.

In a recent development, il costo dei cartellini è relativamente basso al netto, appunto, degli acquisti di questa stagione. Immettere nuove risorse significa potere lavorare diversamente. Ed è anche il motivo per cui potrebbe arrivare Tresoldi: sarebbe un investimento da 12 milioni a stagione: in caso arrivasse la Champions, ecco che sarebbe già ampiamente ripagato.

By CRAIG HOPE, CHIEF FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 14:15 EST, 11 November 2026 | Updated: 16:29 EST, 11 November 2026.

Thomas Tuchel has revealed that Harry Kane is annoyed by team-mates who pull out of England squads – and says his captain would never do so.

Several of the head coach’s camps have been blighted by withdrawals, including Cole Palmer’s ‘load management’ excuse in September. The Chelsea playmaker was then left out of the squad for this week’s Nations League fixtures.

And Tuchel states Kane, who will become England’s record cap-holder with his 126th appearance against Croatia on Thursday evening, is not a fan of those who pass up the opportunity to play for their country.

‘He is always here and doesn’t like it if 50-50 decisions are taken by the players not to come to camp,’ said Tuchel.

‘We had this conversation very early when I took the job and it was one of his points, to make sure that players come and are proud to arrive because it’s the biggest honour.

‘We need to make sure that if it happens (withdrawals) we are so strong that we actually set the tone that everybody is desperate to be in camp, because everybody can lose their shirt if they miss out on a camp.

Thomas Tuchel (centre) has revealed Harry Kane's frustrations at his team-mates pulling out the England squad.

Cole Palmer (right), pictured with Kane in 2024, has been criticised by Tuchel for missing too many England opportunities.

‘So it was one of the first discussions and straight away he set the standard and made it very clear where the standards are for him. He would never pull out. Never.’.

Kane, meanwhile, claims his desire burns brighter than ever as he targets 100 England goals and records that will stand for generations.

He insists he is far from finished and has warned team-mates Declan Rice and Jude Bellingham that his caps record could yet reach 150.

‘This is no time to rest,’ stated Kane. ‘I've got better year on year. While I'm feeling like this, why would I put any limit on myself? I want to get 100 England goals as rapidly as possible.

‘Jude and Dec, they're on 60-odd caps already and you look at how young they are. So I'll try and give them a good number to catch! Before we know it, it’ll be the home Euros. I might be on 140 caps by then, and then we'll be talking about 150. My biggest fear is finishing my career and thinking I could have done a bit more. I have an ego to be the best. I just don't do it in a show-off way.’.

This change accounts for about half of the fall in the country’s fertility rate during the 1990s.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LEWIS BROWNING, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 16:04 EST, 11 November 2026 | Updated: 17:13 EST, 11 November 2026.

Former Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola will be the United States' top target to replace Mauricio Pochettino if and when their manager joins Manchester United, according to a report.

It is looking more and more likely that the former Tottenham and Chelsea boss will take over from Michael Carrick at Old Trafford in the coming days.

Pochettino is presently with his United States Men's National Team players ahead of their fixtures against Haiti in the CONCACAF Nations League this fortnight, but is expected to join up with United after those games.

That will leave the United States needing a new boss and, according to The Athletic, they will set their sights on Guardiola.

The Spaniard is renowned as one of the best managers around, having won the Champions League and six Premier League titles while with City.

He also has historic success with Bayern Munich and Barcelona, and has previously shown interest in potentially moving into international football.

The United States are reportedly set to make Pep Guardiola (pictured) their top target to replace Mauricio Pochettino as manager.

Pochettino (right) is set to leave his role at the USMNT to take over at Manchester United.

As recently as the summer, Guardiola  came so close to being appointed Italy manager that he was 'writing down line-ups' before ultimately deciding not to take the role on.

He was touted to take over an under-performing Italian national team, but the move fell through, and Italian Football Federation technical director and defensive legend Paolo Maldini resigned after a move to appoint Andrea Pirlo also collapsed due to his commercial links with a Russian betting firm.

Maldini opened up on how close Guardiola came to taking over the team, revealing that the Spaniard was seemingly on board for a pretty long time.

'(Guardiola) is the coach who best embodies technical, attacking football,' Maldini told Corriere della Sera. 'He had expressed the idea of wanting to coach a national team to some friends.

'We went to meet him in Barcelona, we had lunch together, we talked for an entire day.

'He was very tempted. He came very close to accepting. He even started writing line-ups down on sheets of paper.'.

Sources indicate that it is reported that Guardiola has spoken to officials at the US national side in the past and is intrigued by working in America. He lived in Newly introduced York briefly after leaving Barcelona in 2012.

He is said to have been approached in 2024 before Pochettino was appointed, and wished the Argentine well upon his appointment.

Pochettino is at the moment away with the States but is likely to join United in the coming days.

Sources indicate that he said: 'I wish him and the USA - I have friends there - the best of luck. I know he's a top-class manager.'.

It has been revealed that he has also been previously quoted as saying: 'The USA is fascinating to try and build a project for many years and being able to get the national team to the next step. The potential with the USA is there for the amount of people and sports and so on.'.

United moved closer to putting Pochettino in charge at Old Trafford after reaching a verbal agreement with the US national team boss on Wednesday.

Meanwhile, the club's chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox were in Monaco where minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe was expected to ratify their decision to sack Carrick with the blessing of co-chairmen Joel and Avram Glazer.

Carrick's departure could be confirmed on Thursday, but official confirmation of Pochettino's appointment may take a little longer with more talks planned overnight on Wednesday.

Published: 17:30 EST, 11 November 2026 | Updated: 17:47 EST, 11 November 2026.

From a distance, it was difficult not to look at the fall-out from Ryan Porteous’ rash challenge on Ilkay Gundogan in the opening match of Euro 2024 and draw sweeping conclusions.

Coming on the cusp of half-time in the Allianz Arena, the defender’s two-footed lunge on the German midfielder earned him a straight red card with a two-game suspension soon following.

According to recent reports, the moment of madness led to Kai Havertz giving the host nation a three-goal lead from the penalty spot at the interval. By time-up, Steve Clarke’s depleted side had lost 5-1. The self-belief which they’d brought into the tournament was fast evaporating, too.

Recent findings suggest that while no one doubted the scale of the task Scotland faced before a ball was kicked that evening, Porteous’ actions made the mission impossible. As a consequence, the former Hibernian defender found forgiveness hard to come by.

Those irate Scotland supporters who demanded that he suffered for his folly were granted their wish.

A player who’d featured in seven of the eight qualifiers disappeared from view thereafter, briefly emerging from international exile as a sub against Greece in March of last year, yet posted missing again throughout the World Cup qualifiers and from the tournament itself.

Ryan Porteous' red card gave Scotland a mountain to climb in Euro 2024 defeat to Germany.

It seemed only logical to deduce that Clarke had also shared the anger of the Tartan Army and that the player’s status as a pariah was down to his simmering fury at the humiliation that woeful tackle caused.

Porteous always believed the matter wasn’t quite as clear cut as most imagine it to be.

‘I think people maybe read too much into that,’ stated the 27-year-old.

‘In the conversations I had with Steve after the Euros and in the next qualifying campaign, the red card against Germany never came up.

‘We had loads of conversations, both when I was in and out of the squad.

‘Those are the things that people obviously don’t see.

According to recent reports, ‘They maybe think Steve Clarke is the type of person who wouldn’t phone you or text you. But he did. We spoke loads to be honest. He was really honest with me.

‘I texted him when he left the role and he messaged back eager to see me get back in the squad.

The Scotland defender was shown a straight red for this challenge on Ilkay Gundogan.

‘Everyone knows Steve is a manager who, if he picks a squad and they do well for them and they get to a tournament, he’s loyal.

‘In terms of the conversations we had during those latter stages of qualification, he just told me to keep doing what I was doing.

‘He was honest and told me I would probably need some of those lads to drop off in form if I was going to make it. You have to respect that.

‘I went to a tournament in the Euros in 2024 and you had someone like John Souttar who missed out. So, I know what it feels like on both sides.’.

Porteous, to his credit, doesn’t appear to be bitter about how matters unfolded post-Germany.

Regardless of the true importance of the red card in his status changing from mainstay to that of an outcast, he accepts that fairness and the game do not always walk hand-in-hand.

‘That happens in football, it’s just one of those things,’ he shrugged.

‘I’ve had a career where I’m up and down, I’m left and right, you just need to bounce back from it.

‘It was a fantastic experience for me to be part of that run we went on. It helped me grow massively. I don’t look at it as being unfair.’.

Porteous has now returned from period in wilderness ahead of North Macedonia clash.

In a recent development, by the time he’d moved from Watford to Los Angeles to sign for LAFC last August, he’d already reconciled himself with the fact that his Scotland career was in cold storage. The consolation was that this afforded him a different perspective on the November night when history was made.

‘It’s maybe tough when the squads were getting confirmed and then a couple of days after that,’ he reflected.

‘But then as soon as you’re watching the games, you just become a fan straight away again and want the team to do well.

In a recent development, ‘I probably hadn’t experienced that for a while. It was actually good for me watching the World Cup qualifiers - because I was able to sit and watch them straight after training because of the time difference.

‘When Kenny McLean scored from the halfway line (against Denmark) I had half the team in LA shouting and screaming for Scotland! It was brilliant.’.

While he’d clearly have preferred to still have been at the heart of things, his new life on the other side of the Atlantic allowed him to sample what it all meant to an invading army in the summer.

‘I had a few days off at one point and I went out to Boston,’ he explained.

‘I didn’t manage to go to the games, but I saw my friends and family who were over and we went to the baseball as well.

‘Being in that fan environment, it just gives you that extra little bit of hunger to get back.’.

Porteous in action for Scots at training as they prepare for North Macedonia showdown.

Industry observers note that the profile of the MLS always offered him that possibility. Porteous’s club counts Gareth Bale and Olivier Giroud among its former players. Son Heung-min is the current star in Tinseltown. The Scot played against - and defeated - Lionel Messi’s Inter Miami in February. In such moments, one can feel a long way from Midlothian.

‘It’s quite mental,’ he smiled.

‘I think I could be the first guy ever to go from Dalkeith to LA! It’s very hot. They are actually choking for a bit of rain just now.

‘I used to blame the East Mains wind for losing my hair, but it’s still falling out over in LA even without the wind.

‘(John) McGinn has already peppered me after seeing a couple of my interviews over there.

‘I’ve had to change my accent so that people can understand me over there.

Recent findings suggest that ‘For the first couple of months, everyone was asking me to repeat myself. But it’s an incredible place and I’m enjoying every second.’.

LAFC finished sixth in the Western Conference this year, good enough to book a slot in the forthcoming play-offs.

Porteous’ part in that meant he was firmly in Sebastien Pocognoli’s thoughts when Stephen Welsh suffered an untimely injury ahead of the two final Nations League matches.

Over two years on from that hideous night in Munich, this feels like a deserved opportunity to change the narrative which has surrounded him ever since.

‘People pay their money and they can have their opinions on me,’ he mentioned.

‘I’ve got thick skin now. It’s never been an problem for me in terms of managers having to pull me aside and have a word or anything like that.

‘I’m in a good place now. Whatever criticism I get, it only makes me grow stronger as a person.

‘Hopefully, I can come back now a better player than what people saw before.

‘I have still got my strengths and I feel like I’ve added to my game as well from being in different leagues and different environments.’.

Birmingham City have seen Phil Neumann star in their rise to the top of the Championship table. The German defender has grown into a key figure in his second season with BCFC, and his performances are not going unnoticed.

In a recent development, amid links with Nottingham Forest and Fiorentina, Neumann has now been quizzed on his future in an interview with Transfermarkt. While maintaining the belief that he can play at a higher level, he insisted that his full focus is on the Blues’ promotion push. He noted: “Of course I hear about those kinds of reports, but I don’t pay much attention to them. I have my advisors for that, people I trust who handle those matters.

Recent findings suggest that “My full focus is on Birmingham City and what we’ve set out to achieve as a team. There’s nothing more notable to me than doing everything I can to achieve our goals with the club. We have a massive task ahead of us, and that’s where I’m concentrating all my energy. Everything else is secondary at the moment.”.

In a recent development, neumann is under contract at St Andrew’s until 2028. He later went on to say that if he was to leave the Blues, “the whole package would have to be right”.

In a recent development, standout players in the Championship often have eyes on moves to the next level. In recent years, those to establish themselves in the second tier before making notable steps up include Hayden Hackney, Shea Charles and Borja Sainz.

It has been revealed that the level of Neumann’s performances for Birmingham City suggests that he may be one of the next Championship aces to earn a move to a higher level. But, his words show that he has nothing on his mind other than the Blues’ ongoing promotion push.

The commitment to the cause he has shown in his response to rumours is aligned with the heart he’s showing on his pitch. Neumann embodies how this BCFC side are all pulling in the same direction to achieve their goal after a challenging 2025/26 season.

It is exactly what the fans were asking for as the club look to reach their lofty targets.

At 29, Neumann will feel that he needs to take a chance to play in the top flight sooner rather than later. The clear aim is to do so with Birmingham City, but interested clubs could offer him a route to a higher level if the Blues can’t make it.

According to recent reports, given the centre-back’s comments, it would be a surprise – and a substantial blow – to see him leave mid-season. You have to feel it would be the perfect package for both him and BCFC to sway them into a deal.

Recent findings suggest that if Chris Davies‘ side can’t make it to the Premier League this season though, the chances of Neumann leaving will grow. He will be in the last year of his contract, and there will be sides ready to offer him a shot at a higher level.

For now though, Neumann’s full focus is on the promotion push at St Andrew’s.

  • In a recent development, per allontanare qualsiasi altra minaccia esterna e mandare un messaggio forte alle pretendenti di Lautaro, l'Inter ha intenzione di estendere il contratto del "Toro".
  • Lautaro manca dal 17 ottobre, dopo aver saltato 7 partite per infortunio subito lo scorso 13 ottobre contro il Bruges in Champions League.

Non basta un contratto fino al 2029? Evidentemente no, per questo l'Inter starebbe meditando di prolungare l'accordo con il suo capitano, Lautaro Martinez, per confermare la volontà di un investimento a lungo termine e senza cessioni. Questo a discapito degli interessamenti massicci del Barcellona mostrati in estate, al punto che il club blaugrana ha contattato l'entourage dell'argentino per portarlo in Catalogna dopo la scottatura per il mancato approdo di Julian Alvarez. Niente, la società nerazzurra si è messa di mezzo perché lo ritiene fondamentale in questo momento nella squadra di Cristian Chivu. Da giocatore più pagato in Italia dopo il rinnovo di ormai due anni fa, guadagna 11 milioni di euro annui.

In a recent development, per allontanare qualsiasi altra minaccia esterna e mandare un messaggio forte alle pretendenti di Lautaro, l'Inter ha intenzione di estendere il contratto del "Toro". Prossimamente, la dirigenza di viale della Liberazione vorrebbe legarlo al club fino al 2032 circa. Avrebbe allora 33 anni di età, il che lo proietterebbe sempre più vicino a trascorrere il resto della sua carriera all'Inter.

Lautaro manca dal 17 ottobre, dopo aver saltato 7 partite per infortunio subito lo scorso 13 ottobre contro il Bruges in Champions League. Un problema muscolare che lo ha tenuto fuori per tutto questo tempo e che gli ha impedito di viaggiare con l'Argentina per gli impegni in amichevole con il resto dei compagni. Ma ora è sul punto di rientrare, dopo aver approfittato della sosta nazionali per recuperare la forma. Resta da capire se potrà già mettere piede in campo a gara in corso contro l'Atalanta alla ripresa del campionato. Un totale di 7 partite, 6 gol e un assist tra tutte le competizioni, nazionali e di coppe. Tra l'ambizione di ripetersi con lo Scudetto in Italia e quella Champions mancata in due finali.

Max Dowman-mania could make League Cup hottest ticket in town

📅 15 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 28 min read (5557 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~28 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that there is an obligation on all of us, from supporters to pundits and journalists, to remain calm and measured about footballers as young as Max Dowman.
  • "The hype will only continue to grow!"Max Dowman that is delightful!
  • According to recent reports, at this rate, Arsenal supporters will be looking forward to Carabao Cup matches as eagerly as any Premier League or Champions League game, simply because it will be a chance to watch Dowman again.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that there is an obligation on all of us, from supporters to pundits and journalists, to remain calm and measured about footballers as young as Max Dowman. But, my word, he does make it difficult. Arsenal’s 16-year-old sensation continues to sparkle whenever he steps on to the field, and he did so again with this superb display against Ipswich Town.

"The hype will only continue to grow!"Max Dowman that is delightful! 👏 pic.twitter.com/UfFY1VSyXn.

According to recent reports, at this rate, Arsenal supporters will be looking forward to Carabao Cup matches as eagerly as any Premier League or Champions League game, simply because it will be a chance to watch Dowman again. The forward’s age and inexperience means he is still used sparingly in those high-priority competitions. The League Cup, by contrast, may prove to be his domain over the coming months.

Dowman’s double at Portman Road made him just the second 16-year-old to score two goals in a game for a Premier League side. The first was Wayne Rooney, for Everton against Wrexham in 2002.

Sources indicate that the two goals underlined why there is so much excitement around Dowman. The first was a demonstration of his prodigious dribbling ability, as he weaved through Ipswich’s defence and buried his shot with the weaker right foot. The second indicated his composure: a slotted finish, rolled in with ease.

Recent findings suggest that max Dowman nets his second of the game! 😍 pic.twitter.com/XRZ9GqZx3x.

As Mikel Arteta approaches the point of signing a new contract in north London, one wonders how much the idea of developing Dowman will excite him as he looks to the future. Which manager would not want to coach a player of such natural ability? Which manager would not want to see how good he could be? The same is true of Marli Salmon, the 17-year-old defender who also impressed on Tuesday night.

It has been revealed that “A joy to have him,” stated Arteta of Dowman. “It’s remarkable. It’s something very natural for him. He can deliver those actions effortlessly, I would say. What we have to do is look after him. He is 16. You don’t see that in this league. In other leagues in Europe, that’s a totally different context.

According to recent reports, “Having two teenagers playing for Arsenal at this level is so fulfilling. Because I’ve been there and just to be able to contribute to somebody’s career and dream, to be able to experience a game like tonight, is phenomenal. And yeah, medium and long term, we know that if they continue to develop in the way that they are, we are going to have two tremendous footballers.”.

"He was brilliant, he made the difference - we need to look after him" 🌟Mikel Arteta claims Arsenal need to "be really cautious" with 16-year-old Max Dowman after he scored twice in Arsenal's 4-2 win over Ipswich 🔴 pic.twitter.com/1msJAEkK8z.

Dowman’s two goals, along with strikes by Noni Madueke and Mikel Merino, secured a comfortable victory for Arsenal against Premier League opponents. Ipswich scored a goal of their own, through Anis Mehmeti, but never seemed likely to cause the visitors too much bother. A late strike from former Arsenal player Chuba Akpom was only a consolation. “We found a way to fight back into it,” stated Gary O’Neil. “Losing by two goals to them isn’t a dreadful effort.”.

Dowman is already developing a trademark goal, of sorts. His first strike for the club, against Everton last season, came after he left an opponent face-down on the turf at the Emirates Stadium. He inflicted the same pain here upon poor Cédric Kipré, who tried to tackle the teenager in the seventh minute but ended up with a mouthful of grass.

Recent findings suggest that it was an image that encapsulated Arsenal’s dominance in the early exchanges, as was the sight of Madueke firing in the second. The chance came after Bruno Guimarães and Merino, majestic in midfield, had monstered Ipswich’s attempts to play out from the back. Merino was dominant throughout, winning tackles with steel and then spinning away opponents with style. “He’s unbelievable,” said Arteta.

Arsenal’s long-term relationship with the League Cup is not a particularly healthy one. For a club of their stature, it is a source of mild embarrassment that they have not won this competition since 1993. They came close last season, reaching the final at Wembley, but were defeated by Manchester City.

Sources indicate that given the depth of Arteta’s squad, Arsenal really should reach the final again. If this is a tournament for the B-team, at least in these early stages, then Arsenal probably have the best B-team in the country. They started this game without any of Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Martin Odegaard, and Kai Havertz but were still extraordinarily strong in midfield and attack.

According to recent reports, the only pre-match concern was their defence, which has been weakened by a couple of early-season injuries. Arsenal started with Salmon at centre-back and the teenager was in direct combat with the physical, sharp-elbowed threat of Ipswich striker Zian Flemming. He stood up to the challenge with determination and class.

Recent findings suggest that ipswich had made 10 changes following their victory at Crystal Palace at the weekend, which was an indication of where the Carabao Cup sits in their priorities. They were able to get into Arsenal’s penalty area but never gave the impression they could really hurt the Premier League champions, apart from when Mehmeti converted Jack Clarke’s low cross.

Akpom struck in the 91st minute to encourage O’Neil, but by then the game had been lost. Arsenal’s work, and indeed Dowman’s work, had been done.

"He's 16 years old, and we have to be cautious of that" 💫Mikel Arteta reacts to an incredible performance from Max Dowman as Arsenal put FOUR past Ipswich 🔴Don't miss the Carabao Cup on @paramountplus 📺 pic.twitter.com/AIcAbMx6ub.

On managing the hype that surrounds Dowman, Arteta stated: “What we have to do is look after him. He’s 16 years old, you don’t see that in this league. In other leagues in Europe, that’s a totally different context, but in this league, with the demands... We need to make sure that every time we throw him in it’s in the right context with the right preparation.”.

Conor Coady shares his thoughts on Arteta’s role in Dowman’s development:.

"He'll know how to nurture him!" 🗣️Conor Coady says Mikel Arteta is the perfect manager for Max Dowman 👏 pic.twitter.com/YdgLxfKiOf.

In a recent development, asked about Dowman’s two-goal performance, Arteta said: “A joy to have him, Marli [Salmon] as well. Seventeen years old, to play at that level with the physicality they have to be able to handle that level, it’s remarkable. Max, yeah, it’s inevitable to talk about him when he scores and he creates the moments he has created tonight. It’s normal.”.

Sources indicate that he added: “He is coping better and better and better, he did the action where he regains the ball and wins it in the first goal, he loses his man... He’s an unbelievable player because of the character that he has and how much he loves to play on the biggest stage and still handles the situation with such naturality.”.

Speaking in his post-match press conference, Mikel Arteta mentioned: “Really pleased with a lot of things we did tonight, the way we attacked the game, how dominant, fluid and aggressive we were, right from the beginning to try to influence the result. We scored two very early goals that gave us obviously a great platform for the game.

Sources indicate that “Individually some big performances as well. Some debuts tonight which is great to see as well, so we take a lot of positives from tonight.”.

Salmon won the header, and then continued to win the overall battle with Flemming. Such an impressive performance by the 17yo. You don't see many defenders doing that at this age.

Arteta’s side are through to the fourth round of the League Cup.

Recent findings suggest that arsenal are finishing this match with a 16-year-old, 17-year-old and two 18-year-olds on the pitch. A good evening for the academy.

And right on cue, Salmon picks up the ball on the halfway line and drives forward, eventually forcing a foul from Nunez who goes into the book for his troubles.

Gyokeres finally gets a sniff at goal but Greaves is wise to his movement in behind and times a slide-tackle perfectly to poke the ball off for a corner.

Speaking on The Tuesday Club podcast, Davies said Adams revealed his football philosophy to be: “You need seven.”.

The “seven” in question, Adams explained, are seven members of the team who are ready and willing to fight the opposition in the tunnel after the game. Once a team have those seven individuals, Adams said, everything else flows from there.

Recent findings suggest that for much of the past two decades, Arsenal have not had seven. In some years in the latter stages of Arsène Wenger’s tenure, they probably did not even have three or four. But that has all changed in recent seasons under Mikel Arteta, to such an extent that the Premier League champions would now undoubtedly bring considerably more than seven combatants to any touchline scrap or tunnel bust-up.

Saturday’s gritty 2-0 victory away to Sunderland provided evidence that Arsenal have added two more of these characters to their squad this summer.

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of the Carabao Cup third-round tie between Ipswich Town and Arsenal. Mikel Arteta’s side have won all six of their matches so far this season, but travel to Portman Road fresh off an incident-filled win over Sunderland which thrust officiating back into the spotlight after Ezri Konsa conceded a penalty having been – in Arteta’s words – “judo-rolled” by Dan Ballard.

After the match, the Arsenal manager stated: “I watched [the incident] 20 times and I cannot find a way to understand how to even think to give a penalty in this situation or the way the VAR has to intervene. So I don’t know what to think, really. But I’m sad, that we have to discuss, after such a beautiful game, something at this level that has the gravity of that because that changes the course of the season and it can cost you the championship… This cannot happen.”.

Arteta may be pleased that VAR is not in use at this stage of the Carabao Cup, and all eyes will be on Peter Bankes who takes charge of tonight’s match against Ipswich.

According to recent reports, this season Arsenal hope to arrest a startling League Cup record. It has been 33 years since they last lifted the trophy, during which time they have been runners-up seven times. Losing last year’s final will have also added fuel to Arsenal’s fire, and Arteta may resolve he must field a strong starting XI. In fact, he may not have much choice in his backline as Ben White has emerged as a serious injury doubt after picking up an injury at the Stadium of Light and may join Cristhian Mosquera and William Saliba on the treatment table. This would likely mean starting Jurriën Timber, who is only just returning from a long-term groin concern. There is more scope for rotation in advanced positions, with Noni Madueke, Viktor Gyokeres, Eberechi Eze and Mikel Merino contenders to start.

A 90th-minute Zian Flemming winner against Crystal Palace on Saturday helped Gary O’Neil’s Ipswich to their second win in four Premier League games, a feat they required 16 matches to achieve the last time they were in the top flight. Heavy investment into Ipswich’s squad has proved fruitful thus far, though in-form striker Emersonn is expected to sit out tonight having taken a knock at Selhurst Park.

Tech Report: Pocognoli fears Scottish Premiership 'identity crisis' over lack of homegrown stars

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.
  • Published: 17:30 EST, 11 November 2026 | Updated: 17:55 EST, 11 November 2026.
  • Sebastien Pocognoli believes the Premiership has an identity crisis caused by a lack of Scottish players pulling on the jersey at our top clubs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 17:30 EST, 11 November 2026 | Updated: 17:55 EST, 11 November 2026.

Sebastien Pocognoli believes the Premiership has an identity crisis caused by a lack of Scottish players pulling on the jersey at our top clubs.

Just six of the 26 players the newly appointed national team manager initially selected for the Nations League double-header with North Macedonia and Switzerland play their football in this country’s top division.

And while the Belgian understands the attraction and the benefits of top talents moving to some of Europe’s top leagues, he’s concerned that the division which should be his first port of call when it comes to making selections is now a barren land.

‘The Scottish league misses Scottish players in the biggest teams,’ he said.

According to recent reports, ‘The league is intense and competitive, but I am not looking at this. I am looking at who is performing at the big clubs.

In a recent development, ‘I believe that’s the most close to international level. And for that you need to play Champions League, Europa League, Conference League in some stage of the competition.

In a recent development, ‘That is what I’m looking at. I hope that players who are performing well, let’s say in the bottom (half), can bounce to the next step to a top club inside the country.

Pocognoli has been alarmed by the lack of Scottish talent in the SPFL Premiership.

Pocognoli has been impressed by the progress of young Celtic full-back Colby Donovan.

‘That will make the competition more competitive, maybe you will go through after the winter into the Champions League or Europa League.

‘That gives the experience to the young Scottish players and in the end, we’d get the benefit.

‘That’s what I’m looking at more in Scottish football rather than the clubs and the style of play of clubs, that kind of thing.

‘It’s not easy because if you look at the Scottish competition, there’s not many young lads who are getting an opportunity to shine compared to Belgium, France, Germany.’.

The specific problem of a lack of opportunities being afforded to players who are eligible for the Scotland under 21 side was highlighted at the recent summit at St Andrews which all 42 clubs attended.

With Turkey the only nation which currently gives fewer minutes, the SFA’s chief football officer Craig Mulholland has tabled two proposals which would see clubs obliged to offer more chances to emerging talents in both league and cup matches.

Optimistic that such changes to the rules would lead to a brighter picture further down the line, Pocognoli added: ‘Hopefully, we can see the benefits in future.

‘I follow all of the young lads, not only from the Premiership in Scotland, but also the Championship and League One because some of them are on loan.

‘My job is not only to win the next game, it’s also to prepare for what’s coming next season.

It has been revealed that ‘In one year, a lot can change. I try to support all the decisions of the clubs in Scotland regarding the fact they play Scottish players and young ones especially.

‘Colby Donovan is a good example, he played some good games for Celtic and I tried to help to accelerate his progress, then he signed a new contract and plays week after week.

‘He is not selected this time, but I think we will get the benefit later on.

‘For Findlay Curtis it’s the same, he’s not playing a lot at Rangers but I believe in his quality.

‘We need to support those type of players because we need them, but hopefully it can help his pathway at Rangers to get some minutes.

‘I hope some other players will be on the same pathway this season.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Middlesbrough were keen on an ambitious move for the Premier League prospect before missing out on a deal. Boro are right now eyeing promotion to the Premier League from the Championship and they are joint-top of the table after 15 fixtures along with Birmingham City and Stoke City.

It has been revealed that moore, 19, is due to spend the entire season with FC Koln in the Bundesliga but he has struggled to make an impact so far. He has made nine appearances in all competitions since his switch in the last transfer window, eight of which have come in the Bundesliga, but he has managed only one assist and no goals.

In a recent development, according to i News, Boro were interested in a swoop for him ahead of this campaign but they weren’t able to lure him to the Riverside Stadium in the end. Rangers were also in the frame for his signature after his spell at Ibrox last term but Spurs sent him to the RheinEnergieStadion instead.

In a recent development, middlesbrough drew 0-0 away at Watford last time out before the international break. They are back in action this weekend against Bristol City at home.

Sources indicate that moore, who can play as an attacking midfielder or winger, would have been an ideal addition for Middlesbrough. Luring him to the second tier would have been a substantial statement of intent by Boro.

According to recent reports, the England youth international is highly-rated by Spurs and is being tipped for a bright future in the game. He spent last season at Rangers and scored seven goals in 47 matches for the Glasgow giants.

Moore, who is from London, would have injected more quality into Kim Hellberg‘s starting XI. He knows Will Lankshear from their time at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium together and they could have formed a formidable partnership.

According to recent reports, however, it wasn’t to be and Spurs opted to let him join FC Koln in the German top flight instead. Moore has been on the books of his current club for his whole career to date and rose up through their academy ranks.

Moore’s move to FC Koln hasn’t worked out so far. He has taken a bit of time to adapt to life in Germany.

Recent findings suggest that middlesbrough will get the chance to reignite their pursuit down the line. If they get promoted, they could be a perfect next destination for Moore.

Boro are winless in their last two matches and have missed Lankshear up top. They need to return to winning ways on Saturday as they gear up to play out of form Bristol City.

#26378. Latest Update: 'He always wanted to play for Scotland'. Alex McLeish recalls the moment the national team found their fresh talisman in Scott McTominay

📅 11 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1080 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dailymail ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: 'He always wanted to play for Scotland'. Alex McLeish recalls the moment the national team found their fresh talisman in Scott McTominay

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1080 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.
  • Published: 17:30 EST, 11 November 2026 | Updated: 18:02 EST, 11 November 2026.
  • While Alex McLeish’s second stint as Scotland manager clearly did not go to proposal, the compensations from that period proved to be significant for the national team.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 17:30 EST, 11 November 2026 | Updated: 18:02 EST, 11 November 2026.

While Alex McLeish’s second stint as Scotland manager clearly did not go to proposal, the compensations from that period proved to be significant for the national team.

Without a struggling side earning a play-off spot in the Nations League, a famous night in Serbia under Steve Clarke would never have been possible.

According to recent reports, for all we know, the years in international exile may have rolled on. The ongoing improvement which led to participation at the World Cup this summer might never have happened.

McLeish’s greatest legacy, however, was surely to persuade Scott McTominay to pull on a dark blue shirt after he travelled to Carrington in 2018.

Alerted to the Lancaster-born player’s eligibility by then Manchester United manager Jose Mourinho, the man who won 77 caps for his country could have been forgiven for feeling that the coup he pulled off was just never meant to be.

‘The beast from the east,’ McLeish recalled with a grin.

Scott McTominay (left) and Alex McLeish in 2018 ahead of a friendly against Belgium.

McLeish and McTominay together in a Nations League encounter against Albania in 2018.

‘When I was forced off the train in Newcastle, they noted “it’s not going any further, the weather’s knackered.”.

‘So, I had to wait for a train down south. And I thought “at this point will I go home?”.

It has been revealed that ‘And I thought, “no, I’ve come this far, so I’m going all the way”. Then I got to my hotel at five in the morning, the guy states, “oh, I thought you were a no-show, son.”.

‘I noted - “no - I’ve arrived and I’m needing a room.”.

‘I didn’t go in for the breakfast as Mourinho said “just come in at lunchtime, get some food and we’ll have a chat.”.

‘But he mentioned he (McTominay) definitely wants to play for Scotland.

‘So, it was good to hear that from Jose.’.

Mourinho liked what he saw the minute he set eyes on the player. It’s fair to say that not everyone at the club around that time was similarly enthused.

Recent findings suggest that ‘He was still just a kid, quite raw,’ McLeish recalled. ‘But he had the physique, speed and skill on the ball.

According to recent reports, ‘He was good in the air and also with the ball at his feet. It made it a no-brainer.

‘I’d gone to a couple of Man United games and they were just kind of breeding him into the system.

McTominay in training ahead of the Nations League clash against North Macedonia on Friday.

‘Listen, anyone would have done it and brought him into the squad.

‘The only problem we faced was that England were in the frame as well. But when I remarked to Scott, “I’d love you to play for Scotland,” he said “That’s the only team I want to play for.”.

‘And all of a sudden we had a brand new young superstar.’.

Truth be told, it would be some time before Scotland supporters began to place McTominay in such a bracket.

He had his moments early on for his country, but his deployment as a defender – by both McLeish and Clarke – did him no favours.

It was only in the qualifiers to Euro 2024 that the futility of that approach was accepted.

McTominay was outstanding as a central midfielder in the qualifiers, his performance and two goals in the famous win against Spain topping the lot.

Industry observers note that in little over a year, he’d be a Napoli player. And within a season, he’d become a Serie A winner and voted Italy’s best player.

Many Manchester United fans were outraged that the club had sold him for just £25.7million.

Even some England supporters voiced their displeasure about the player slipping through their hands.

‘They have such a massive pot to pick from in England,’ McLeish reflected.

‘But I’m sure that privately, in some of their chats behind the scenes, they will have said ‘we should have got McTominay.’.

‘But he chose Scotland. He wanted to to come. He wasn’t saying anything about England at all.

‘And that was the best news I could have got in that era of rebuild.’.

While Clarke rightly got the plaudits for taking the team to three tournaments, McLeish has taken a huge amount of pride from the part McTominay has played in it all.

‘It’s incredible how he’s grown and grown,’ he added.

‘In the first few games, he was just trying to feel his way into the international scene. But he gave everything from that first call-up.

Scott McTominay in action against Haiti in the 2026 World Cup.

‘He’s played in just about every position in the team down the years. He was in the back four at one stage.

‘But he’s mainly operated in the middle of the field and he’s a real threat in the box and moving from middle to front.

‘The way he runs with the ball is just superb because he really knows what he’s doing.

‘He’s got massive confidence and I hope that a lot of young Scottish players coming into the game can take inspiration from what Scott has done.'.

In a rare media conference this week, McTominay put his underwhelming displays at the World Cup in context.

Two days before the opener against Haiti in Boston, he underwent a controlled electric shock in hospital to restore a normal heart rhythm. Since then, he’s undergone a medical procedure to deal with the arrhythmia.

He returns to the Scotland squad a month after pulling on a Napoli shirt again against Frosinone.

With five goals in his past six matches, it feels like the player the Tartan Army grew to love is back with them.

Sebastien Pocognoli may soon feel he owes McLeish a word of thanks, too.

‘It’ll be a massive relief for the manager to get Scott back into the squad,’ he remarked.

‘You always want your best players available.

‘I remember back in my day, going to Kazakhstan when we had a lot of boys missing.

It has been revealed that ‘We were held in a bit of limbo. So, for Sebastien to get players into his team of that level will be massive for him. It could make a huge difference for Scotland.’.

#26376. Sebastian Berhalter makes ‘promise’ to Middlesbrough fans amid £4.3m man’s tough start to life on Teesside

Sebastian Berhalter makes ‘promise’ to Middlesbrough fans amid £4.3m man’s tough start to life on Teesside

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (559 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that middlesbrough signed Rokas Pukstas from Hajduk Split for £4.3m in the summer transfer window.
  • Sources indicate that the slow start is an obvious source of frustration, but one man backing Pukstas to come good is fellow summer signing and compatriot Sebastian Berhalter.
  • Industry observers note that “Once he gets back from his injury, he’s only going to come back better,” Berhalter noted.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that middlesbrough signed Rokas Pukstas from Hajduk Split for £4.3m in the summer transfer window. Boro saw off interest from Birmingham City to land the attacking midfielder, but he has not had the impact hoped with only two senior appearances before injury hit.

Sources indicate that the slow start is an obvious source of frustration, but one man backing Pukstas to come good is fellow summer signing and compatriot Sebastian Berhalter. As quoted by The Northern Echo, he expressed that Pukstas needs time to adjust and develop at only 22 before making a promise to the Riverside Stadium faithful.

Industry observers note that “Once he gets back from his injury, he’s only going to come back better,” Berhalter noted. “He works so hard; he’s one of the hardest-working guys I’ve ever met and he’s going to be just fine, I promise you that.”.

Pukstas’ two substitute appearances have brought just 12 minutes on the pitch for Middlesbrough. He was unused on the bench in four Championship games before his hamstring injury hit, so supporters haven’t really had a chance to see what he’ll bring to Kim Hellberg‘s side.

Sources indicate that the 22-year-old mainly operates in attacking midfield, offering a box-crashing threat as he powers into the box with well-timed runs to have efforts on goal. He has played in a deeper role before too though, as his physical traits translate to duel success and ability on the ball means he can be trusted in possession.

Industry observers note that his well-rounded skillset and physical profile mean he is ideal for Hellberg’s flexible tactics. Expect to see him covering plenty of ground and popping up in both thirds, much like his supportive compatriot Berhalter.

His age means there is plenty of time for Pukstas to grow too. He needs time to get back up to fitness and settle into the Boro side, but Berhalter’s faith is well placed.

Sources indicate that understandably. Pukstas’ limited impact has brought some pessimism from sections of the Middlesbrough support. The fact he barely played before picking up an injury means they are yet to see why £4.3m was spent on him.

Sources indicate that however, the success of Boro’s recruitment means that they have good reason to have faith he will come good on his price. Berhalter’s message should only increase the confidence that the American ace can deliver, but it also serves as a timely reminder that he may need time to show his best as he develops as well.

At present, the expectation is that Pukstas will not be able to return from his hamstring injury until December. Hellberg will likely offer a fresh update ahead of Boro’s clash with Bristol City this Saturday.

Latest Update: USA pulls out of U-17 World Cup just days before it starts… amid war in the Middle East and 'risk of armed conflict'

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (486 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Dailymail

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 18:48 EST, 11 November 2026 | Updated: 18:48 EST, 11 November 2026.
  • The US Soccer Federation is withdrawing its team from the FIFA U-17 World Cup in Qatar amid growing security concern over the ongoing conflicts in the Middle East, according to multiple reports.
  • The American State Department at the moment has a travel advisory for the country at a Level 3, with guidance telling travelers to 'reconsider travel to Qatar due to risk of armed conflict.'.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JAKE FENNER, US SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 18:48 EST, 11 November 2026 | Updated: 18:48 EST, 11 November 2026.

The US Soccer Federation is withdrawing its team from the FIFA U-17 World Cup in Qatar amid growing security concern over the ongoing conflicts in the Middle East, according to multiple reports.

The American State Department at the moment has a travel advisory for the country at a Level 3, with guidance telling travelers to 'reconsider travel to Qatar due to risk of armed conflict.'.

Athletes who were set to compete in the tournament - held from November 19 to December 13 - were informed of the decision via an e-mail.

'We are writing to inform you of the difficult decision to cancel our World Cup pre-camp and our planned participation in the World Cup,' the letter stated.

'We are extremely proud of the preparation by our players and coaches to represent the US in the World Cup.

In a recent development, 'Unfortunately, in light of current circumstances including the US State Department's Level 3 Travel Advisory for Qatar and related directives for Embassy staff and families, we are no longer able to participate in the tournament. The well-being of our players and staff will always be our top priority.'.

The United States has told players they will not participate in the FIFA U-17 World Cup in Qatar.

The US State Department has a Level 3 travel advisory for the country amid ongoing conflicts.

The USA won their CONCACAF qualifying group in order to reach the tournament.

Recent findings suggest that this announcement comes one week after coach Alex Aldaz unveiled his roster for the competition. The team was set to take part in a training camp this week at US Soccer's new headquarters outside Atlanta.

Players were set to open their tournament on November 21 with a match against Montenegro. They were also scheduled to face Chile and Algeria.

The United States earned the right to compete in the tournament by winning their group and outlasting the Dominican Republic on goal difference in CONCACAF U-17 World Cup qualifying.

The Baby Nats drew the Dominicans after beating Saint Kitts and Nevis as well as Saint Vincent and the Grenadines.

At last year's tournament, the Americans reached the Round of 32 before being eliminated by Morocco.

Recent findings suggest that the best finish for the United states at the tournament came in Latest Zealand in 1999, when they came fourth - losing to Australia on penalties. Landon Donovan was named as the competition's Best Player.

FIFA made changes to the tournament last year, making it an annual event rather than once every two years. Qatar won the rights to host it from 2025 to 2029.

According to recent reports, it is not clear which team will replace the United States at the tournament. The Daily Mail has contacted FIFA for comment on the matter.

#26357. Breaking: Engineered bacteria are weaning farms away from synthetic fertilizers

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (829 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nature ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: Engineered bacteria are weaning farms away from synthetic fertilizers

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (829 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that scientists are engineering bacteria that can provide nitrogen, an essential ingredient for plant growth, to wheat crops.
  • The world’s farms depend on synthetic nitrogen fertilizers to increase crop yields, but the production and use of these chemicals generates billions of tonnes of greenhouse-gas emissions every year.
  • Industry observers note that this approach takes a cue from natural bacteria that ‘fix’ nitrogen into a useful form and provide it to certain plants.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that scientists are engineering bacteria that can provide nitrogen, an essential ingredient for plant growth, to wheat crops. Credit: Shakeel Ahmed/Anadolu Agency/Getty.

The world’s farms depend on synthetic nitrogen fertilizers to increase crop yields, but the production and use of these chemicals generates billions of tonnes of greenhouse-gas emissions every year. Now, scientists are making progress on a greener alternative: bioengineered bacteria.

Industry observers note that this approach takes a cue from natural bacteria that ‘fix’ nitrogen into a useful form and provide it to certain plants. Scientists are engineering genetic features into bacteria with the aim of enabling them to fix nitrogen for vital food crops, such as maize (corn) and wheat, that don’t have such natural microbial partners.

In a recent development, in a comment published on 10 November in Nature Biotechnology1, researchers suggest that bioengineered bacteria could eventually replace up to half of synthetic fertilizers. The bacteria deliver nitrogen more efficiently to roots than synthetic fertilizers do, which could reduce greenhouse-gas emissions and nitrogen pollution of waterways. But this would require a slew of advances, from getting different microbial species to work together to more-rigorous field trials.

How CRISPR could yield the next blockbuster cropSome of these ‘biofertilizers’ have been augmented with genes and genetic snippets from viruses or distantly related bacteria. This means that the engineered microbes are classified as transgenic — altered to include DNA from other species. The bacteria are now being trialled on small plots of maize on farms in the Midwestern United States. The bacteria, developed by Switch Bioworks in San Carlos, California, are the first example of a transgenic biofertilizer approved for testing on fields in the country.

How CRISPR could yield the next blockbuster crop.

According to recent reports, in September, Switch Bioworks received approval from the Brazilian regulatory agency, the National Technical Commission on Biosafety (CNTBio), to test its strains there. This is the first time that a transgenic bacterium of any kind has been approved for field tests in Brazil, says molecular biologist Mario Murakami, who is the president of CTNBio in Campinas.

Sources indicate that companies that have focused on editing bacterial genes rather than producing transgenic microbes are further along. Pivot Bio in Minneapolis, Minnesota, has applied its gene-edited biofertilizers to tens of millions of hectares of US farmland over the past decade, claims the company’s chief technology officer Travis Frey. Some of Pivot Bio’s products have also been tested in Canada, Argentina, Kenya and Brazil.

Most plants can’t use the form of nitrogen that is present in the air. Some crops, including soya beans and peanuts, host colonies of bacteria that can convert atmospheric nitrogen into a usable form. The plant takes up that nitrogen and, in return, provides carbon that fuels bacterial growth. But most staple crops lack these microbial partners, leading farmers to rely on synthetic nitrogen fertilizers. These chemical fertilizers account for 5% of global greenhouse-gas emissions, and drive damaging nutrient pollution in waterways.

In a recent development, for decades, researchers have tried to get bacteria to fix nitrogen for staple crops. Until recently, the approach was to collect wild strains of nitrogen-fixing bacteria from soil and apply them to seeds or spray them onto plants. “It doesn’t work,” says Jean-Michel Ané, a bioengineer at the University of Wisconsin–Madison, who is working on microbial fertilizers. The wild microbes fail to thrive when applied to crops that don’t provide them with carbon.

How to climate-proof crops: scientists say the secret’s in the dirt.
