The joke goes that Michael Carrick has already bettered Ruben Amorim’s efforts by reaching the third round of the League Cup, but Manchester United will need to find a way past free-flowing Brighton if they are to go any further.

United were eliminated in the second round by League Two Grimsby Town last season, but start the competition a stage later because they are one of nine Premier League clubs playing in European competition.

Brighton knocked United out of the FA Cup in the third round, with Danny Welbeck scoring at Old Trafford, meaning the club played just 40 matches in 2025-26.

Carrick will want to make a better fist of the cup competitions, but he could really use a win of any kind after taking just four points from United’s first four league games of the upcoming season.

The no-show at Hull and derby defeat by City’s 10 men were especially dispiriting, and the relationship between the club and supporters is becoming increasingly strained.

There were no flags on the Stretford End for the game against City, as fans voiced their opposition to what they view as a heavy-handed ticketing policy. The club notes the measures are to stop ticket-touting but critics believe many innocent season-ticket holders are being caught in the crossfire and having their tickets revoked.

Discontent is never too far away given the continued presence of the Glazer family, and confidence is fragile regarding the club’s sporting direction under Sir Jim Ratcliffe and Ineos.

The news that 15-year-old JJ Gabriel, possibly the country’s outstanding academy player in his year group, wants out (broken by Matt Law in a Telegraph Sport exclusive) nagged at some of those fears. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A major issue for Watford this campaign has been the midfield. The summer departure of Imran Louza was a major blow, with his technical qualities, set-piece delivery and ability to dictate games sorely missed.

It has been revealed that similarly, Giorgi Chakvetadze’s transfer to Udinese has left the Hornets devoid of a creative spark, with his tendency to drift centrally and unlock defences. The club have simply not recruited adequate replacements, and they are suffering for it.

Industry observers note that the current midfield options at Vicarage Road consist of Hector Kyprianou, Edo Kayembe, Edoardo Bove, and recent signing Martin Payero. None of these options are particularly offensive or astute going forward, lacking the ball-carrying and forward-thinking impetus of Chakvetadze, and the game-changing potential of Louza.

In order for Watford to change their fortunes this season, the club’s hierarchy need to address the glaring issues in midfield. Here, we put forward three targets the Hornets should consider moving for ahead of the January transfer window.

Patrick Kelly had a breakout season for Barnsley in 2025/26, establishing himself as one of League One’s most exciting prospects. He was touted for a potential step up, but stayed put and has remained a standout at Oakwell.

Recent findings suggest that A busy and energetic player, Kelly could well offer Watford the spark they need in midfield. His excellent dribbling and physical attributes would complement a side in need of inspiration and dynamism. He ranks among the top 10% of players in his position League One for dribbles completed (FotMob).

Barnsley have had a disastrous start to the current campaign, and as such, a cut-price deal for the 22 year old could tempt clubs further up the footballing ladder.

Sources indicate that bate has been a critical part of highflying Stockport County’s success this season. The diminutive playmaker has contributed four assists and started all but one of the Hatters’ league games this campaign. He excels with his technical ability, ball retention and progression, and eye for a pass.

Having put behind him his injury challenges from last season, he appears to have recaptured his impressive form from the 2024/45 campaign, cementing himself as a potential coup for alert Championship sides.

It has been revealed that at 24 years of age, he represents a good blend of experience and potential to improve further. His position as club captain further demonstrates the leadership qualities necessary to navigate a Championship relegation scrap, which may await at Watford.

It has been revealed that hull City’s promotion and busy summer window has left players such as Kieran Dowell with limited minutes, opening the door to a potential exit. Dowell has been omitted from the Tigers’ Premier League squad, and the prospect of a January exit appears increasingly likely.

Industry observers note that dowell has donned the colours of six different Championship clubs, and has developed a reputation for scoring spectacular goals, as well as being an apt creator and technician. With three promotions at this level, he has the necessary pedigree and experience.

Out of contract in the summer, Dowell would represent a cost-effective option on either a short-term deal or a loan. His lack of playing time in recent seasons is a potential concern, but should he regain match fitness promptly he could be a useful addition to a threadbare Watford midfield.

It has been revealed that as Watford seek to steer clear of the Championship’s lower reaches, bolstering the midfield is of high importance. The only summer addition in this area, Martin Payero, has been underwhelming when given the opportunity.

The fitness issues plaguing Edoardo Bove, the most talented player of the current options, has further stunted Watford’s progress.

The January window offers the club a chance to make amends for poor summer transfer business and to provide the squad with the best opportunity to consolidate their Championship status. The three midfield options put forward would help to push the club in the right direction.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Man United legend Rio Ferdinand has called for 'a face' to explain the decision to sack Michael Carrick after comparing the club's statement announcing his dismissal to ChatGPT.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By MICHAEL PAVITT, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 07:20 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 07:22 EST, 12 November 2026.

Man United legend Rio Ferdinand has called for 'a face' to explain the decision to sack Michael Carrick after comparing the club's statement announcing his dismissal to ChatGPT.

Carrick's dismissal was confirmed in a 142-word statement released at 10.37am, which was sent out by Man United's communications department.

Sources indicate that man United have moved closer to appointing former Tottenham and Chelsea boss Mauricio Pochettino after reaching a verbal agreement with the US national team boss on Wednesday. The club then made a formal approach to US Soccer.

Man United's key decision makers, including chief executive Omar Berrada and technical director Jason Wilcox, have not issued a message following the decision to part ways with Carrick.

Ferdinand, who played alongside Carrick at Man United, has called for officials to front up to the decision in a post on social media.

Recent findings suggest that 'Man United statement like Chat GPT… I wanna hear a voice!' Ferdinand wrote. 'I want to see a face to this…'.

Michael Carrick - pictured arriving at Carrington on Thursday morning - has been sacked after Manchester United's disastrous start to the season.

Man United's leadership, including minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe, chief executive Omar Berrada and technical director Jason Wilcox, were not named in the club's statement.

Man United legend Rio Ferdinand called for 'a face' to speak about the decision after comparing the club's statement to ChatGPT.

Man United's club statement confirming the decision read: 'Manchester United can confirm that Michael Carrick has departed his role as men’s first-team head coach.

'Michael rejoined the club in January and guided the team to a third-placed Premier League finish by winning 12 out of the remaining 17 games of the 2025/26 season, accumulating the highest points tally in the league during that period.

'After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions.

'Michael is, and always will be, a Manchester United legend. Just as he did as a player, he has conducted himself with the highest standards of dedication and professionalism throughout his time back with the club. His leadership and achievements last season will always be fondly remembered.

'The club intends to appoint a permanent successor as swiftly as possible.'.

Minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe, along with the Glazer family, who dialled in virtually from the United States, Berrada and Wilcox reached a verdict in the south of France yesterday, all while Carrick remained in limbo back in Manchester.

Sources indicate that carrick arrived at United's training ground at 7.50am this morning and was dismissed. He left at 10.18am, less than two and a half hours later.

United States boss Mauricio Pochettino is ready to take over as United's newly introduced manager.

Ferdinand, speaking on Rio Presents, claimed Carrick had been disrespected in the way his dismissal had been handled.

'You do everything you can to make this end in the most amicable and respectful and pleasant way possible,' Ferdinand said.

According to recent reports, 'I think the way it has been done, it could have been done better. I think the leaks coming out of the club are terrible, they don't reflect well on anybody at all.

'It adds to the disrespect to the person in charge at the time. It is terrible to play out in the public like this. The minimum you should get is a bit of respect.'.

Carrick leaves with a record of 14 wins – 12 of which came last season, prior to being made permanent manager – six draws and eight defeats, including exiting this season's Carabao Cup at the first hurdle against Brighton at Old Trafford.

Michael Carrick is SACKED by Man United: Manager leaves training ground just 2½ hours after arriving - and now Mauricio Pochettino is ready to take over

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 05:22 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 07:34 EST, 12 November 2026.
  • Michael Carrick has been sacked by Manchester United, with former Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur boss Mauricio Pochettino waiting in the wings as his successor.
  • Just 173 days on from Carrick being given a two-year contract, having guided United to a third-placed finish and back into the Champions League as an interim, the decision to fire him was ratified at a crucial board meeting in Monaco on Wednesday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 05:22 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 07:34 EST, 12 November 2026.

Michael Carrick has been sacked by Manchester United, with former Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur boss Mauricio Pochettino waiting in the wings as his successor.

Just 173 days on from Carrick being given a two-year contract, having guided United to a third-placed finish and back into the Champions League as an interim, the decision to fire him was ratified at a crucial board meeting in Monaco on Wednesday.

According to recent reports, carrick arrived at United's training ground at 7.50am this morning and was dismissed. He left at 10.18am, less than two and a half hours later. He is the first Premier League manager to be sacked this season, followed hours later by bottom-of-the-table Crystal Palace boss Pierre Sage.

Recent findings suggest that in a statement released at 10.37am, Carrick's sacking was confirmed. United's statement read: 'After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions.

'Michael is, and always will be, a Manchester United legend. Just as he did as a player, he has conducted himself with the highest standards of dedication and professionalism throughout his time back with the club. His leadership and achievements last season will always be fondly remembered.'.

It has been revealed that sources close to United say the club's leadership believe their squad of players is far better than the performances and results under Carrick have indicated. They gave the under-fire manager a chance to turn things around against Chelsea, Roma and Aston Villa but ultimately felt the team were not on the right path.

Michael Carrick - pictured arriving at Carrington on Thursday morning - has been sacked after Manchester United's disastrous start to the season.

Carrick was seen leaving the training ground less than two and a half hours later.

USMNT boss Mauricio Pochettino is ready to take over as United's new manager.

Minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe, along with the Glazer family, who dialled in virtually from the United States, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox reached a verdict in the south of France yesterday, all while Carrick remained in limbo back in Manchester.

Carrick took charge of training on Tuesday morning after it had emerged that Berrada and Wilcox were heading to Monaco to recommend his sacking and did so again on Wednesday when it transpired United were closing in on an agreement to bring in Pochettino as his successor.

The current United States national team manager reached a verbal agreement with Man United to take over on Wednesday. United then made a formal approach to US Soccer shortly after, with the club having to trigger the 54-year-old Argentine's £7million release clause.

The final nail in Carrick’s coffin came in Sunday's dramatic 4-4 draw against Aston Villa, which saw United stuck in the relegation zone in 18th position.

The handling of Carrick’s departure has been particularly damning on Ineos and the shot-callers at United, not least given he was given no show of public support when he continued in post following an emergency board meeting after the 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth.

A defeat at Chelsea, in which Lisandro Martinez badly let his manager down by getting sent off, and a win over Roma to go with the draw against Villa, was not enough of a sign that it will turn around for the board to keep faith.

With Carrick's departure, it pushes the compensation paid out to coaching staff and executives over the last three years under minority owner Ratcliffe and Ineos close to £30million. Buying Pochettino out of his contract with the US national team will cost another £7m. Adding his large coaching staff will take millions more.

Matchgoing supporters will be sad to see Carrick go and made those feelings clear in recent games when he was loudly cheered at the end of matches, with the ire and frustration levelled against players and executives.

Optimism heading into the campaign was sky high given that no team in the Premier League performed better than Carrick's side between January and May.

But that level of success and dominance has long since evaporated after a shambolic start to the current campaign - and it has cost the 45-year-old his job just five months after the ink dried on a upcoming deal.

It has been a season in which United won just three matches, one of which came against Azerbaijani minnows FK Sabah, and are yet to keep a clean sheet in the league all season.

A season in which club captain Bruno Fernandes publicly questioned his manager's tactics and Martinez eviscerated the hierarchy for hanging Carrick and the players out to dry. Fernandes was even dropped for the first time in five years for the Bournemouth humiliation.

Questions will continue to be asked of those upstairs, with Berrada and Wilcox now on to their third permanent manager this year alone and their fourth in their tenure having burned through Erik ten Hag, Ruben Amorim and Carrick since taking control of football operations in February 2024.

It means Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox (pictured on Thursday morning) need a third manager this year as INEOS' running of the football club comes under scrutiny once more.

Sunday's draw with Aston Villa proved to be the final nail in the coffin for the United boss.

Gary Neville believes Michael Carrick will be 'disgusted' by his Manchester United players.

Amorim lasted 14 months in the role, even in spite of embarrassing defeats to the likes of League Two Grimsby Town, but for Carrick it was a dream job that would run until early November and end in him being unceremoniously dumped at the training ground by Wilcox.

Recent findings suggest that carrick vowed after the Villa draw that he wouldn’t walk away and took on a spiky side when quizzed on his future by reporters. After a week of shame against the board, he has finally been put out of his misery.

Carrick leaves with a record of 14 wins - 12 of which came last season, prior to being made permanent manager - six draws and eight defeats, including exiting this season's Carabao Cup at the first hurdle against Brighton at Old Trafford.

Now it looks set to be Pochettino’s challenge to turn this massively underperforming squad around, something former United star Gary Neville believes is a mightily difficult task given the 'unprofessional' squad the new man will inherit.

'They've teased him, haven't they? They've conned [Carrick] for a few months. They have, they've conned him,' Neville said on his Sky Sports podcast recently.

'Honestly, he would never say this publicly because he's got class. I can say it for him though.

'He'll look at those players with disgust. Some of them, he'll be disgusted with some of those players.

It has been revealed that 'A few of them aren't that professional. I live in Manchester. Some of them aren't that professional. So I've got no time for them.

'There's a few of them that don't go to bed at the right time, don't eat the right things, don't think about Manchester United every single minute of every day, and aren't living and breathing this football club as they should be - and as professionals should.

'Why? Because it's gone to their heads. They are nothing, some of those players.

Sources indicate that 'He's not been able to get a tune out of them and they've turned on him. I know that because if Bruno has turned on him publicly, with that little statement, imagine what they're like behind the scenes.

'If that's your captain saying that, imagine what they're saying in the dressing room behind closed doors when no one's listening. That's horrific.'.

Tom Garratt has suggested that Blackpool must replace Ian Evatt, as he criticised the manager for the number of ‘excuses’ he comes up with following their defeat at Wimbledon.

The 44-year-old, who had a successful time as a player at Bloomfield Road, returned to the club as head coach in October last year.

Evatt inherited a team in a mess, as the Seasiders had picked up just nine points from 13 games, which had left them bottom of League One.

However, the former Bolton chief inspired a turnaround, and after finishing the season with six wins in seven, Blackpool ultimately secured a mid-table finish.

Therefore, fans went into the current season with hopes that they could kick-on, but it has been a difficult first few months for Evatt and the players, as they are only outside the relegation zone on goal difference.

The latest defeat, a seventh in 13 games, came on Saturday, as AFC Wimbledon beat Blackpool 1-0 at Plough Lane.

Yet, speaking on The Pyramid Podcast, pundit Garratt revealed that he felt this was another example of Evatt refusing to take responsibility this season, as he questioned the approach of the Blackpool chief about how he deals with the media, as well as stating a change in the dugout might be needed.

Either way, Blackpool fans are becoming increasingly annoyed at how this season is playing out, and many will agree with Garratt’s assessment.

There is a feeling that Evatt doesn’t take responsibility, which he must do as the head coach, as he is picking the team and working on the approach all week.

The Glazers took control of Manchester United in 2005. That takeover has since caused so many disruptions and protests by the fans over massive debts and insufficient backing of the team in the transfer market, despite successful periods in the Premier League and Europe.

Now Manchester United need to think about who should control the club in the future. Laurie Whitwell has now shared his views on why Manchester United need an ownership change. He simply wants the Glazers gone from Old Trafford. However, he also recognizes that replacing the current ownership doesn’t automatically mean things will improve for United.

According to recent reports, the journalist believes the change in ownership has had a lasting effect on United, with the club still feeling its consequences today. A fresh start might be welcome, but the identity of the next owners would matter just as much as the departure of the existing ones.

“Personally, I would like to see the Glazers gone from Manchester United,” Laurie Whitwell said on The Rest is Football podcast with Gary Lineker.

“That change, you know, just really affected and still impacts United now.”.

The desire for different ownership is one thing, but finding people capable of taking the club forward is another.

Whitwell admitted there is no perfect answer when it comes to who should take charge.

Sources indicate that that leaves United facing a difficult choice. A sale could offer the chance to change how the club is run, but simply bringing in a fresh owner would not guarantee better decisions or a brighter future.

Whitwell also raised the idea of United supporters having a greater say in the club’s ownership and decisions, much like the Barcelona model where fans own the club itself. However, he highlighted that the Barcelona model isn’t ideal either and has its own shortcomings.

Changing the names at the top would only be one part of the change. The club would also need an ownership structure capable of making sound decisions and providing a direction.

According to recent reports, the glitch of ownership goes beyond whether the Glazers should stay or leave. Manchester United needs to find the right people and the right model to secure the club’s future. Getting that decision wrong could leave them facing the same circus the fans are enduring under the Glazers.

Birmingham City defender Phil Neumann has broken his silence after a fresh round of transfer speculation recently came to the fore involving the German centre-back.

Neumann has been one of Blues' standout performers so far this season as Chris Davies' side sit top of the Championship, with the division returning to action this weekend after the final international break of 2026.

Birmingham's recent form of six wins in seven games whilst boasting the second tier's meanest defensive record further highlights a vast improvement on last season's 10th-placed finish, with Neumann one of many players in the Second City who struggled for overall consistency in 2025/26.

That didn't stop the 6"3 figure from becoming the subject of transfer interest in January and, indeed, the summer window, although it is apparent Neumann isn't giving recent exit talk much thought at this moment in time, which will appease the Blues fanbase and Davies in equal measure.

Neumann, 29, officially signed for Birmingham on last season's July 1st start date, having penned a pre-contract agreement during his final months with 2.Bundesliga outfit, Hannover 96.

In his first Championship season, the towering centre-back featured 32 times in a defence which changed personnel on several occasions, but has been an ever-present this term alongside captain, Christoph Klarer.

Neumann attracted interest from Sassuolo in January and then from Premier League newcomers, Hull City and Bundesliga side, Borussia Mönchengladbach in the summer, but remained at St. Andrew's to aid Blues' flying start to the season.

After also netting twice against Wrexham in August, the defender recently became the subject of interest from Nottingham Forest and Fiorentina, before further links emerged over potential moves to Hull, Coventry City and Ipswich Town as early as January.

The Recklinghausen-born man has never featured in a top European division in his career so far, making 190 appearances in 2. Bundesliga for the likes of Hannover and Holstein Kiel, as well as his 47 Championship outings.

Speaking to Transfermarkt, Neumann admits that the Championship's physical nature has certainly brought the best out of him, whilst also reaffirming his commitment towards the cause of helping Blues realise their promotion ambitions despite the strong exit talk.

"Of course I hear about those kinds of reports, but I don't pay much attention to them. I have my advisors for that, people I trust who handle those matters," he mentioned.

According to recent reports, "My full focus is on Birmingham City and what we've set out to achieve as a team. There's nothing more crucial to me than doing everything I can to achieve our goals with the club.

It has been revealed that "We have a big task ahead of us, and that's where I'm concentrating all my energy. Everything else is secondary at the moment," Neumann stated.

Blues fans, are you reassured about Phil Neumann's immediate future given these comments? Comment below!

"I'm in a good sporting position. Therefore, if I were to consider another option, the whole package would have to be right.

"The league is a factor, but by no means the only one. I want to know what role I'm expected to play, how the coach wants us to play, and what the club's future holds.".

The way in which Davies has altered Birmingham's style this season has clearly suited Neumann down to the ground, as well as the fact he has played all 1,350 Championship minutes.

It has been debated whether he would receive such numbers at the City Ground, despite the fact Forest could benefit from extra defensive depth due to Oliver Glasner's three-back system.

It is also clear that, at this stage of his career, Neumann is one of several players who are excited about what the future holds for Birmingham, including the planned move to the Powerhouse Stadium.

Whether he sees out the next five years in the West Midlands remains to be seen, but the chance of becoming a cult figure by helping return the club to the top-flight is unsurprisingly a major factor in his thought process.

The Argentinian defender has also apologized to the United higher ups as well over his comments, as shared by Fabrizio Romano.

Lisandro Martinez has held discussions with Jason Wilcox and Michael Carrick after speaking out following United’s 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid.

Martinez had questioned whether Carrick was backed enough in the summer and suggested the club needed changes.

Fabrizio Romano has now confirmed that United consider the matter resolved for now and expect Martinez to remain available for selection.

Speaking about the situation on his YouTube channel, as quoted by Football 365, Romano explained why Martinez’s comments caused concern inside the club.

“He spoke very strongly after the game against Atletico Madrid, which Man Utd lost. It was a very negative moment for the Red Devils. We know that Licha was very strong in his comments. He said that Michael Carrick was not backed enough during the summer transfer window.”.

Romano added that Martinez had spoken directly to those at the club after the incident.

“Licha apologised to Man Utd as a club. He spoke to the directors, he spoke to Jason Wilcox, and he spoke to Michael Carrick, who was also involved in this conversation.”.

“So, the underlying message remains the same. Lisandro is apologising for the way he expressed himself after a game during a difficult moment for Man Utd, but there was a discussion about the substance of what he stated.”.

Romano also revealed that United had imposed a financial penalty on the centre-back. However, the punishment does not appear to involve removing him from the squad.

“According to the information available tonight, Lisandro Martinez has been fined.”.

He added that Martinez is expected to return to the squad as normal, with the fine considered sufficient punishment for the incident.

It has been revealed that “The internal discussion also helped to resolve all the issues. For Man Utd, the case is closed.”.

That should bring some immediate clarity to the situation, although questions remain about how the episode could affect Martinez’s longer-term position at Old Trafford.

Romano also pointed towards Martinez’s contract, which expires next summer, with United holding an option to extend it.

“So, let’s see what is going to happen there. For sure, this is the kind of situation that will have an impact on the situation surrounding Lisandro, but we have to see what happens next in terms of future transfers and everything else.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There was very much a Samba beat to this Manchester City victory – and it almost had a famous father in the crowd up dancing.

This was a night when Brazilian Allan Elias scored his first goal on an enterprising first appearance for City.

But it was another debutant who stole the show as the Carabao Cup holders sailed past Norwich City to set up a fourth-round meeting with Brighton.

Floyd Samba scored two fine goals and had a hand in another on a dream debut that had his beaming dad up off his seat and thrusting his arms in the air as if ready to party.

If the Samba surname feels familiar, that is because Floyd’s father Christopher played more than 200 games for Blackburn Rovers, Queens Park Rangers and Aston Villa.

In fact, it was very much a family affair as Floyd’s brothers Tyrone and Emerson, who are also in City’s academy and hoping one day to tread a similar path, joined in the jubilant celebrations alongside their mother, a visibly emotional Theresa.

According to recent reports, this particular evening belonged to Floyd, though. Deployed as a lone striker by Enzo Maresca, you would not have known he ordinarily plays as a midfielder such was the confidence and composure the 17-year-old oozed.

Norwich could not live with him or City for that matter as Maresca’s impressive start as manager since replacing Pep Guardiola continued apace.

Industry observers note that this must have been an incredibly satisfying moment for Samba Sr. He came through incredible hardship – at one stage as a teenager he was rough-sleeping – to forge an impressive career totalling more than 450 games for club and country.

So to be in a position to now have three sons in City’s academy and one produce a debut like this will fill him with enormous pride. Floyd was later seen enjoying a warm embrace with his dad in the crowd, moments after being congratulated by Tyrone, a year his senior, and 12-year-old Emerson, who plays for City’s Under-13s.

Industry observers note that “I knew there would be an opportunity to get some minutes for the first time with the first team – to get a debut like that is mind blowing,” Samba said. “I couldn’t believe it myself, but that’s just the beginning, I’ve got a massive career ahead of me. It was a great debut.”.

Floyd caught the eye with a fine free-kick in City’s 2-1 FA Youth Cup final victory over Manchester United last season and now he has goals for the senior side to his name. Pretty stunning they were, too.

The first was a superbly steered header past two Norwich bodies on the line from Allan’s cross and the second a lovely, nonchalantly curled finish low into the far corner.

It has been revealed that what a moment for Floyd Samba! 😍A goal on his Man City debut for the 17-year-old, son of former Blackburn defender Chris 🩵 pic.twitter.com/VCVfX9HCNn.

Chris Samba has deliberately kept a low profile, keen to let his sons get on with their own careers free of distractions, but there was no chance he was going to be able to suppress his emotions in that instant. And nor should he. It was some moment for the boy and his family.

As impressed as Maresca was by the goals, it will have been other elements of Samba’s game that also caught the eye. He did extremely well to hold off the attentions of Norwich’s centre-backs when receiving a pass from Ayyoub Bouaddi and then returning the ball to the Moroccan who released Rayan Cherki through to score City’s second. His movement was also sharp, at one point taking a difficult pass sweetly in an adjusted strike, only for Norwich’s Bruno Alves to come across to make a timely intervention before Samba could get his shot off.

"Was there any doubt?"Ayyoub Bouaddi with his first assist for Man City as he sets up Rayan Cherki to make it 2-0 🔵 pic.twitter.com/0gfxp5GDXy.

It has been revealed that “It was satisfying not just for the two goals but for the entire performance,” Maresca noted. “He didn’t play many games as a nine but he was good. He’s young, full of energy, strong, he can finish.”.

According to recent reports, allan, a £34m summer signing from Palmeiras, will have been just as pleased with his contribution. Maresca’s fluid formation initially resembled a 3-1-5-1 with Allan effectively operating as a right wing-back but he stuck doggedly to the task before eventually getting the moment to showcase his quality, first with his cross for Samba and later with a neat solo run and finish.

Driving inside Sam Field and then cutting back inside the Norwich man before curling an inch perfect finish into the bottom corner – all of it done with his left foot – it was quite the introduction.

In a recent development, allan on his debut! 🇧🇷Magic from the Brazilian to make it 3-0 to Man City 💥 pic.twitter.com/nw6lNqh1yL.

Hugo Viana, City’s director of football, has remarked supporters will need to be patient with Allan and that it may take the 22-year-old time to adjust to English football but this first outing will do his confidence plenty of good.

“It was notable for him to play 90 minutes and to see a little bit the English competition that is a bit different from South America so overall was good,” Maresca said.

Cherki was the only survivor from the team that started Sunday’s victory over Manchester United but it all felt pretty seamless from City. Bouaddi, the £85m signing from Lille, was poised and graceful in midfield alongside the impressive Mateo Kovacic and Geronimo Rulli could not have asked for a much quieter debut in goal.

Recent findings suggest that FLOYD SAMBA again!! 🌟The 17-year-old curls one in to score his second on his Man City debut with his dad Christopher watching on in the stands 👏 pic.twitter.com/fJ5mfEWBx1.

Recent findings suggest that nico O’Reilly looked like he had barely broken a sweat despite Norwich’s players routinely being unable to keep up with him. Norwich themselves made nine changes but the gulf in class was enormous and testament to City’s strength in depth.

The game also gave Maresca the opportunity to give run outs to two more academy graduates who played in that Youth Cup final triumph, Kaden Braithwaite and Ryan McAidoo and the latter got his own name on the scoresheet to make it 5-0.

Recent findings suggest that all told there were seven City academy graduates on the pitch, two of them playing for Norwich. This was certainly a night to remember for the club’s youth production line.

According to recent reports, with the dominant performance, Man City have earned themselves the privilege of hosting Brighton in the next round, who will no doubt prove a much stiffer challenge than Norwich. They become the sixth all-Premier League tie in the next round, with only Fleetwood, Bradford and Peterborough remaining from outside the top flight:.

According to recent reports, erling Haaland left out of the squad, watching from the stands, would have enjoyed that performance from Floyd Samba. Here is his second goal for you to enjoy on his debut night:.

FLOYD SAMBA again!! 🌟The 17-year-old curls one in to score his second on his Man City debut with his dad Christopher watching on in the stands 👏 pic.twitter.com/fJ5mfEWBx1.

Five unanswered goals and a home-grown hero emerges for Manchester City!

It has been revealed that great through ball from O’Reilly, which Lewis lets run past him for the dummy. McAidoo runs on to it on the right of the box and first-time fires it low into the far corner.

It has been a perfect night for Manchester City’s academy.

Industry observers note that well we look like we’re heading for a matching scoreline to the previous edition of the fixture. That pesky shot on target is still eluding Norwich, whereas Samba is still out there looking for his hat-trick.

Two minutes of time to be added – who will get there first?

O’Reilly sends a high, looping ball to the back post from the left side, where McAidoo rushes to meet it but can’t get over it under pressure.

Final change for Norwich, as Kvistgaarden who has not had much service tonight, comes off for Schwartau.

Mo Touré strays just offside on the edge of the box, as Musaba sends a lovely little ball over to find him on the turn and the forward slots it past Rulli. Celebrations don’t quite begin before the flag goes up but that is a shame for the visitors.

Norwich have managed to get more of a grip in this half, despite conceding two more goals, but they are still without a shot on goal as we approach the final 15 minutes.

Man City take off scorer of their third goal Allan to bring on Braithwaite.

Norwich replace Ben Slimane and Bruno Alves with Touré and McConville.

Samba again at the heart of the action, laying off the ball to McAidoo on the right for the winger to run into the box. His shot towards the far post is saved low by Grimshaw who spills it almost into the path of Lewis, but Norwich survive.

Lewis makes a run down the right-hand side and crosses into Samba on the edge of the box. He lays off to McAidoo, but his shot goes sailing over the bar.

A surprise to no one, it is chucking it down in Manchester.

It has been revealed that big cheers from the away end as Norwich get their first corner of the evening. It is lofted high and long to the back post, where it is headed away by Bouaddi. It bounces out to Musaba, who has just come on, and he strikes it from the top of the box on the half-volley.

His shot cuts through a crowd in the box and has Rulli diving to his left, but it goes wide of the post. What an introduction that would have been!

Sources indicate that well all the stories from this match will be all about young Floyd Samba. Feel free to leave your best punny Samba/dance-related headlines in the comments section.

For Man City as you would expect it is all about game management from here on out.

Some more changes to report for Norwich as well, as Crnac is replaced by Musaba.

In a recent development, what a way to score a second! A night to remember for Floyd Samba!

Norwich try and play out from the back but far too sloppy and Ait-Nouri picks up the ball on the left of the box. He has plenty of time to tee up Samba inside the box at the left corner, who finds himself with plenty of space to curl his shot into the far corner, beating the diving Grimshaw.

We may be seeing plenty more of him this season.

Recent findings suggest that norwich looking for their way back into the game, as the ball comes down the left, fizzed in low and flashes past Rulli, trying to claim it. It deflects off a crowd of bodies and spins up, but Fisher can’t connect and it spins away harmlessly wide of the goal.

Norwich take off Diallo for Maghoma.

45 minutes left for the visitors to create something special!

What a moment for Floyd Samba! 😍A goal on his Man City debut for the 17-year-old, son of former Blackburn defender Chris 🩵 pic.twitter.com/VCVfX9HCNn.

Manchester City will be the ones to host Brighton in the next round – giving the visitors the opportunity to pull off a remarkable feat of knocking out both Manchester sides should they win.

Enjoy the highlights from last night as they came from behind to dispatch Man Utd:.

Defending set-pieces and counter-attacks has been a persistent problem for Sage’s side, and he won just two of his ten Premier League games in charge.

Pierre Sage has been sacked by Crystal Palace after a dismal start to the season saw them win just two of their first ten games.

Palace sit rock bottom of the Premier League, their leaky defence having conceded 24 goals.

Daily Mail Sport understands many players voiced fears they were being pushed too hard in training, with sessions the day before a game particularly intense. There were also significant concerns about the quality of Sage's backroom staff, with his assistant Jamal Alioui proving especially unpopular among the players.

Sources indicate that there has also been considerable turnover among senior executives, with six departures over the past 18 months. Chief financial officer Mitesh Velani is set to add to that number in the coming months. One well-placed source told Daily Mail Sport that the disruption to the club’s business operations has the hallmarks of a club heading for relegation.

As Palace look to bail themselves out of trouble, Daily Mail Sport understands talks are progressing with former Brentford and Tottenham boss Thomas Frank, who is expected to take over ahead of crucial games against Coventry and Hull after the international break.

Industry observers note that palace chairman Steve Parish first contemplated sacking Sage over his lack of defensive nous in September, but gave him a stay of execution after Palace kept a clean sheet in a spirited performance away at Leeds on the eve of the international break. However, that display proved an anomaly as Palace shipped 19 goals in the following nine games.

Palace have won just once in their last eight matches in all competitions, beating Fulham 1-0 in the fourth round of the Carabao Cup.

In September, Daily Mail Sport revealed tensions had emerged between Sage and Parish when the latter took a dim view of the decision to drop teenage defender Jaydee Canvot for their defeat by Ipswich Town.

According to recent reports, palace paid French club RC Lens £4million in compensation to appoint Sage in June after he won the French Cup, finished second in Ligue 1 behind Paris Saint-Germain and was named manager of the season last term. Palace players found Sage’s training sessions too intense and struggled to adapt to the late schedule.

Succeeding Oliver Glasner, Palace's greatest manager, proved too big a task for Sage.

Following Palace's loss to Liverpool, Sage insisted the Eagles have been playing better than their league position suggests and pleaded for more time. Those appeals fell on deaf ears.

It has been revealed that 'A lot of times I’ve mentioned we deserved better and it was the case again (on Sunday),' said Sage. 'My job is not the most key thing, as I always said from the beginning. The most important thing is to find an efficient solution for the team and for the club.

‘We have to adjust some positions during the winter transfer window to give more solutions and more efficiency and I think it will be OK.’.

#26237. Retractions of old papers are on the rise: when should bad science be culled?

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 14m • 📚 Deep Dive (2727 w)
📖 Baca
General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Nature ↗ Open Full Page

Retractions of old papers are on the rise: when should bad science be culled?

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 14 min read (2727 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, in August 1987, a scandal erupted over work on the world’s highest mountain range.
  • More than 10,000 research papers were retracted in 2023 — a latest record.
  • More than 10,000 research papers were retracted in 2023 — a new record.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Illustration by Piotr Kowalczyk.

In a recent development, in August 1987, a scandal erupted over work on the world’s highest mountain range. John Talent, a palaeontologist at Macquarie University in Sydney, Australia, declared he had found numerous anomalies in research charting the geology of the Himalayas. All of the problems were in papers by Vishwa Jit Gupta, one of India’s most celebrated palaeontologists at the time.

More than 10,000 research papers were retracted in 2023 — a latest record.

More than 10,000 research papers were retracted in 2023 — a new record.

Gupta was outraged. But further investigations over the following seven years revealed the scale and brazenness of his fraud. Littered through more than 450 publications were maps of collection sites that didn’t exist, plagiarized images and specimens stolen from collections that Gupta had visited. More than 100 experts had been duped into co-authoring descriptions of fossils Gupta claimed he had collected from specific Himalayan geological formations, but instead hailed from North America and Morocco.

“It destroyed the image of Indian science,” states retired geologist Ghulam Bhat, who completed his PhD on Himalayan geology in the same year that the allegations of fraud emerged.

Gupta died in 2022, and many geologists know to steer clear of his work. But awareness of the problem is fading, and none of Gupta’s papers have been retracted. When Nature contacted Bhat, who is now editor-in-chief of the Journal of the Geological Society of India (JGSI), he was unaware that Gupta’s papers were not marked as retracted. That’s despite the JGSI’s 1991 evaluation of 19 of Gupta’s papers that it published1, which concluded that “the fossil finds of V. J. Gupta are not reliable [...] the data is incomplete bordering on disinformation”.

Much of Gupta’s work is inaccessible, having been published in now-defunct periodicals or in volumes that, although digitized online, have not been indexed in reference bibliometric databases such as Scopus, Web of Science and Dimensions. Despite this, Gupta’s falsehoods are now being propagated outside specialist circles, as his old journal articles are being surfaced through artificial-intelligence tools that summarize search results. When someone searches for geological landmarks in the Himalayas, such as the Tandi Limestone, Google’s AI overview obliges with direct links to Gupta’s discredited papers.

Bhat now intends to rectify the digital record and indicates that all other journals that have published Gupta’s work should do the same. “If this problem is left as it is, unattended, it will pollute all of the geological literature in future,” he says. Gupta also published papers in Nature in the 1960s; Chris Graf, director of research integrity at Springer Nature, didn’t confirm that the journal would re-examine them. But he added that in general, when investigations of old papers are hampered by limited available information, an editorial expression of concern “is likely to be our preferred mechanism for alerting readers to potential concerns”. (Nature’s news team is editorially independent of its publisher, Springer Nature.).

The Himalayas case raises a wider issue: how to deal with fraudulent, unethical or even merely incorrect research from decades ago, especially in an era in which much old work is digitized and AI systems can pick up studies that might previously have been neglected.

There are many skeletons in science’s closet, but publishers can be reluctant to judge science of the past by today’s standards, and can find it more difficult to issue retractions when authors are dead, original records cannot be consulted or journals are no longer in print.

And as publishers struggle to deal with the fallout from rising research fraud and AI slop, finite resources can also mean that many old papers with known flaws are left as they are.

Gráinne McNamara, a council member of the Committee on Publication Ethics (COPE) in Eastleigh, UK, which advises journals on best practice, claims that journals are increasingly contacting COPE to ask for advice about dealing with concerns on very old papers.

“Everybody is looking for what’s the best, most responsible way to handle these,” she claims.

In a recent development, the widespread use of retractions as a mechanism for maintaining integrity in the scientific record is a relatively recent phenomenon. The JGSI evaluation report about Gupta served as a warning notice to the community at the time, but didn’t use the word retraction. It also pre-dates the modern standardization of retraction processes, which happened in the 2000s. Now, a journal should concern a retraction notice, and leave the original paper intact, but with a modified title and a stamp or watermark indicating that it has been retracted. The information should then feed through to bibliographic databases.

According to recent reports, in the early 2000s, only around 30 retraction notices were published each year, and COPE first developed guidelines to standardize the retraction process in 2004. The number — and rate — of retractions has exploded since then, with more than 10,000 recorded in 2023 alone.

It has been revealed that digitization of old records, combined with a wider propensity to retract flawed work, has seen journals reaching farther back in time to retract studies — and this has led to some startlingly long gaps between when an article was published and when it was formally retracted. Retraction Watch, an initiative that curates a database of more than 70,000 retractions and expressions of concern (a notice that highlights potential issues with a publication), has reported that the longest gap is 80 years. That’s for a prank case report published in 1923 in the Dutch medical journal Nederlands Tijdschrift voor Geneeskunde.

It described a man who died from “piss cough”, an affliction that caused him to cough up liquid smelling of urine. In 2003, an editor at the journal happened to look up the case, which he thought was widely known to be a hoax. Realizing it had never been retracted and that others did not know it was fake, he sought confirmation of the hoax, and found it in the autobiography of a retired University of Amsterdam physician, who had helped to cook up the nonsense case when he was a medical student. Accompanying commentary on the journal’s website said that a retraction was appropriate now that the older literature had become accessible through digitization.

According to Nature’s analysis of Retraction Watch data — which capture a subset of total retractions — the number of old papers that are being retracted is rising. Overall, some 358 retraction notices and 120 expressions of concern have been issued for papers or book chapters that were more than 20 years old at the time of the editorial action (see ‘Retracting the past’). This is still a rare phenomenon: since 2015, the oldest retractions represent some 0.7% of the total number, up from 0.2% before 2010. But around 3% of expressions of concern have occurred for works older than 20 years. That illustrates how publishers might choose to issue expressions of concern for older papers, rather than retract, because it can be harder to investigate historical records.

According to recent reports, in 2005, biochemist Barry Milborrow sought to retract five of his own papers, published between 1980 and 1982, on biochemical pathways that bacteria, algae and plants use to make pigments, because later work had disproved their findings. The Biochemical Journal, which published Milborrow’s self-retraction listing the five articles2, retracted both articles it had published. Another journal issued a correction, but no notice was issued by the publisher of the remaining two papers. Ian Swift, Milborrow’s co-author and PhD student at the University of Upcoming South Wales in Sydney, Australia, at the time, states he only found out about the retractions many years later, after Milborrow had passed away.

In a recent development, according to COPE guidance, journal editors can retract articles if they no longer have confidence in the results and conclusions reported in them. By that rubric, many older papers could, in theory, be retracted, but, being rarely cited, are usually left alone.

According to recent reports, even when invalid papers are still being cited, retraction might not follow. In 1985, for instance, geneticist Svante Pääbo reported that he had cloned DNA from an Egyptian mummy3. The seminal work marked the birth of palaeogenomics, a field that earned Pääbo a Nobel prize in 2022. But the mummy DNA was actually contamination from a modern handler, as Pääbo, now at the Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology in Leipzig, Germany, has openly acknowledged. “What is problematic is if false conclusions lead other scientists and the community as a whole astray,” he told Nature when asked for this article. “I don’t think anyone is right now misled by the mummy paper,” he notes, which is why he argues that the work should stand, adding that to correct very old papers with errors “would create more confusion than clarity”.

Retractions can reshape scientists’ careers in unexpected ways.

Retractions can reshape scientists’ careers in unexpected ways.

According to recent reports, in practice, old papers tend to be considered for retraction only if they have widespread integrity challenges that journal editors feel shouldn’t be allowed to stand unmarked. A major trigger for mass retractions of older work is when investigations of an individual’s research cast doubt over their entire body of work. For instance, a 2019 investigation by King’s College London into the work of psychologist Hans Eysenck and his German collaborator Ronald Grossarth-Maticek has led to papers dating back to the 1940s being flagged — albeit many with expressions of concern rather than retractions.

In a recent development, eysenck died in 1997 as one of the most celebrated psychologists of the twentieth century. But in 2019, psychiatrist Anthony Pelosi, who had critiqued Eysenck’s work to no effect in the 1990s, published a renewed analysis of the studies4. An accompanying editorial called on King’s College London — where Eysenck worked from 1955 until 1983 — to conduct a formal investigation. The investigation report, also published in 2019, concluded that 24 articles by Eysenck and Maticek published between 1988 and 2000 were ‘unsafe’ and recommended they be retracted.

In a recent development, those recommendations weren’t followed entirely. Only 16 of the 24 papers have been retracted, and another 4 have expressions of concern. Four remain unflagged. After sustained criticism over the narrow scope of the 2019 investigation, King’s College London published a statement in October 2025 saying that other publications based on the data set used in the 24 papers it examined are also likely to be ‘unsafe’ and should be flagged by journal editors — although it did not list affected publications.

So far, 94 of Eysenck’s hundreds of papers have been either retracted or tagged with an expression of concern, the oldest of which was published in 1943 (see ‘Longest gaps’).

Recent findings suggest that such inconsistencies in how publishers deal with research-integrity challenges are common and don’t relate only to very old papers, states Andrew Grey, an endocrinologist and research-integrity specialist at the University of Auckland in New Zealand. He alerted publishers to concerns over large numbers of articles by Yoshihiro Sato, a Japanese bone-health researcher who fabricated data in dozens of clinical trials, and has reported seeing some journals respond with retractions or expressions of concern, whereas others take no action5.

Recent findings suggest that one famous scandal of the past — the 1980s discrediting of work by John Darsee, a US biologist — has led to just 17 retractions. Although news reports at the time stated that more than 80 of Darsee’s papers had been retracted, this refers to editorial notes and warnings that, in parallel with the Gupta case, don’t appear in modern records as retractions.

Another trigger for retracting old work is when it attracts renewed attention, particularly in medical fields.

Sources indicate that each year, Marcel van der Heyden, a physiologist at the University Medical Center Utrecht in the Netherlands, asks his final-year students to write a review article about a poison or toxin. In 2025, he chose caesium salts, and his students uncovered 20 case reports of people ingesting the toxic chemical6. Often, the individuals deliberately consumed the compound as an alternative treatment for cancer. Although the US Food and Drug Administration cautioned against its use in 2018, the deadly ‘therapy’ is still promoted in books and online by some wellness centres.

The treatment traces back to two papers published in 1984 in Pharmacology Biochemistry and Behavior. One of the papers was written by Austrian-born Hellfried Sartori, who had been prosecuted in Maryland in 1982 for fraud relating to using the unproven cancer treatment. That case ended in a mistrial. Sartori subsequently had his medical licence revoked in several US states in the 1980s and was sentenced to prison in Virginia in 1999 for practising medicine without a licence. And in 2010, an inquest into the deaths of five people in Australia found that he had been treating patients remotely from Thailand. Many more of his patients had also died under his treatment, the court heard.

The other paper promoting caesium therapy was by Wisconsin-based Aubrey Keith Brewer. Brewer died in 1986, but his namesake Brewer International Science Library continues to distribute information on caesium and other alternative therapies with a disclaimer that the protocols are “for information purposes only”, and that people should consult their physician if unwell. Nature contacted the website but received no response.

Van der Heyden contacted Pharmacology Biochemistry and Behavior in August 2025, suggesting an expression of concern could be warranted. “Without the original data, it’s hard to tell whether there is a mistake made, or whether it’s on purpose,” he says. But the research-integrity team at the journal’s publisher, Elsevier, decided in January this year to remove the two papers, soon after Van der Heyden informed them that his review had been accepted for publication and that his university was poised to issue a press release about it. The papers were deleted entirely this April, as Retraction Watch reported.

The move to scrub a paper, rather than merely retract and leave it in place, can be taken if the contents could present a serious health risk to the public, according to COPE guidelines.

Leeds United welcome Manchester United to Elland Road on Sunday, with both sides looking to put a difficult run of results behind them and get their Premier League season on track.

Leeds United suffered a 2-1 defeat away to Arsenal last weekend despite James Justin scoring to put them in front in the 55th minute.

Manchester United also dropped points in the Premier League, drawing 1-1 with Tottenham, before losing 2-0 to Atletico Madrid in the Champions League away from home.

Michael Carrick’s side have struggled to find consistency in recent weeks and have come under immense pressure to get in results. The Whites meanwhile will hope that home advantage can make the difference when United face their bitter rivals on Elland Road.

It has been revealed that leeds have recorded one win, two draws and two defeats in their last five matches in all competitions. Their best result came against Newcastle, where they won, but a 6-3 defeat to Chelsea in the Carabao Cup and the loss to Arsenal have left them searching for a response.

Sources indicate that manchester United have also won just once in their last five matches. Their 4-0 Champions League victory over Sabah FK was the only comfortable win, but defeats to Manchester City and Atletico Madrid, alongside draws against Fulham and Tottenham, have raised questions about their form and Michael Carrick.

Sources indicate that leeds are waiting on Dan James, who returned from international duty with a back problem and missed the Arsenal game. Joe Rodon remains sidelined with a hamstring injury and is not expected back in full training until next month. Harry Wilson could return after being an unused substitute last weekend. Mateo Joseph is also among Leeds’ absentees.

Manchester United have their own concerns. Luke Shaw and Kobbie Mainoo are doubts after picking up issues against Tottenham and missing Tuesday’s trip to Madrid. Benjamin Sesko remains unavailable with a recurring shin problem, while Patrick Dorgu is expected to be out until late November. Manuel Ugarte is recovering from knee surgery, and Noussair Mazraoui is a doubt with a back problem.

According to recent reports, there is better news regarding Matthijs de Ligt, who could return to contention. Leny Yoro is also available for selection despite his Champions League suspension.

Industry observers note that the match takes place at Elland Road on Sunday, October 18. Kick-off is scheduled for 2 pm BST (1pm GMT).

UK viewers can watch the game live on Sky Sports Main Event, with coverage beginning at 1 pm BST.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Blackburn Rovers may have to go into Sunday's East Lancashire derby against Burnley without first-choice goalkeeper Balazs Toth, as they sweat the results of a possible broken finger while on international duty with Hungary.

It's been a hectic international break for Blackburn, who went into it sitting 13th in the Championship with 21 points from 15 games. They've punched above their weight all year and have exceeded plenty of pre-season expectations so far.

Toth has helped Rovers stay in games, and at Bristol City especially, win them, making seven saves at Ashton Gate and preventing 2.56 goals in a classic 1-0 away win. His contract is up at the end of the season, so his long-term future is up in the air, but in the meantime, he's an important player at Ewood Park.

So, the possibility of losing him for their biggest game of the campaign on Sunday at Turf Moor against a hapless Burnley side would be a massive blow.

Toth's performances in a Blackburn shirt have led to him nailing down the number one shirt for Hungary. He played every minute in their Nations League campaign, including Tuesday night's draw against Northern Ireland.

That point was enough to see ex-Rovers boss Michael O'Neill lead his side, filled with EFL talents such as Justin Devenny, who scored the equaliser against Hungary, Pierce Charles, Terry Devlin, Isaac Pirce and others, to top Group 2 of League B in the Nations League.

In a recent development, it was a massive result for the Green and White Army, as it means they'll be playing in League A in the next Nations League phase. As for Hungary and Toth, his evening got worse as he revealed he was heading to hospital after the game to treat a possible broken finger.

"I most likely broke my finger. I’m on my way from the stadium to the hospital, hoping it might not be too serious," Toth said in an interview translated from Hungarian after the match.

According to recent reports, "It’s hard to come to terms with the fact that we didn’t win. We got what we expected from Northern Ireland. We didn’t play that well; we couldn’t break them down; perhaps we lacked a bit of creativity.".

Toth and his Hungary side can still earn promotion to League A of the Nations League, with their second-placed finish in their group securing a play-off spot. They'll battle Slovenia, Bosnia and Herzegovina and the Republic of Ireland in March.

It's not been the most encouraging week for Blackburn fans. They were initially worried after talisman Andri Gudjohnsen was substituted at half-time against Luxembourg, although a possible injury concern has since been debunked by Iceland boss Arnar Gunnlaughsson.

Sources indicate that then came the sad news that Tony Mowbray had to step back from his role as head coach due to health concerns. The 62-year-old is loved across the EFL, and has been the man largely credited with Rovers' perceived overachievement so far this season.

And now there's the possibility that Toth may miss the East Lancashire derby and further games due to an injury picked up on international duty.

It has been revealed that "U have got to be kidding me, ☠️," one Blackburn fan commented on X. Another remarked that it was "time to end international breaks forever.".

One other supporter claimed that "the universe doesn't want our club to succeed" while the word "cursed" was thrown around, too.

There were some optimistic fans believing that Toth could possibly play on with a broken finger. He did so for around half an hour during the game on Tuesday night, but adrenaline could have got him through that.

Sources indicate that ainsley Pears played on with a broken wrist at times last season while Toth was out himself, so perhaps the Hungarian can soldier on for the time being. At least, that's what some fans hope.

Blackburn's return to action against Burnley has plenty of anticipation. For the first time in what feels like years, Rovers head into a matchup at Turf Moor as the favourites. They haven't won an East Lancashire derby in over 16 years, but that could end on Sunday.

In each of the last four campaigns they've shared a division, the Clarets have been promoted out of the Championship. Burnley have won seven of the last eight meetings, but they head into this one inside the bottom three with one win all season.

It has been revealed that do you think Burnley could take advantage of the recent news out of the Blackburn Rovers camp to spring a surprise on Sunday? Let us know in the comments.

Sources indicate that more importantly, too, their winless league run at Turf Moor will have eclipsed 400 days come Sunday. Regarding league position and home form, Blackburn have a massive opportunity to earn some rare derby success.

However, these setbacks won't be helping at all, and the last thing Blackburn needs is to head into their biggest game of the season disjointed against a Burnley side who will be as desperate for the win as they ever have been.

Rovers will be hoping that Toth comes out of the hospital unscathed and without a serious injury, as losing him for Sunday could be detrimental to their chances of winning.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chelsea’s World Cup contingent has moved from a group-stage watchlist into a genuine Xabi Alonso planning problem.

Chelsea’s own tournament revision confirms that Enzo Fernandez, Mike Penders, Moises Caicedo, Kendry Paez, Malo Gusto and Jorrel Hato have reached the Round of 32.

England have also progressed after their final Group L win over Panama, which keeps Reece James and Trevoh Chalobah inside the wider knockout picture.

For supporters, that is a status marker. For Alonso, it is where summer pride starts to become pre-season compression.

Sources indicate that the concern is not simply volume. It is where the minutes are landing.

Enzo has not missed a minute for Argentina, while Caicedo has remained central for Ecuador and captained them in the 2-1 win over Germany.

According to recent reports, those are not fringe workloads. They are the two midfield profiles Chelsea have built large parts of their control game around.

Alonso’s first Chelsea pre-season was always going to demand clarity through the middle of the pitch.

Instead, the players most central to that reset are still operating in knockout football.

Caicedo’s Ecuador role is the cleanest example. Read Chelsea has already assessed how his captaincy display against Germany strengthened his leadership case, but the next layer is more complicated.

Every additional knockout tie gives him more tournament rhythm, more authority and more fatigue.

Enzo brings a different tension.

Argentina’s route against Cape Verde keeps him on a glamorous stage at exactly the moment Chelsea need to settle his role, mood and tactical responsibilities under Alonso.

If Madrid-related noise continues around him, the club cannot afford a sluggish July handover.

Then there is the defensive side.

Reece James started England’s first two matches before a hamstring matter ruled him out of the Panama game, according to the Guardian.

England still topped the group and moved into a last-32 tie with DR Congo, but James’ situation is exactly the kind of detail Chelsea’s medical team will monitor closely.

Chelsea have already had to strategy around a large World Cup group.

The broader concern was clear in Read Chelsea’s earlier pre-season workload piece, but the knockout stage sharpens it because the returns will now be staggered.

Recent findings suggest that enzo brings a maximum group-stage load. Caicedo brings captaincy responsibility and heavy Ecuador minutes.

James brings knockout qualification mixed with another hamstring-management question.

Gusto and Hato remain tied to France and the Netherlands, while Penders and Paez are still absorbing tournament environments before club reintegration.

That is a spine issue, not a fringe issue.

Alonso needs automatisms in possession, spacing around the double pivot, clearer full-back behaviour and pressing triggers from midfield.

Those details do not bed in properly when key players arrive in drips after a major summer tournament.

Players returning from knockout football can bring competitive sharpness that closed-door friendlies cannot replicate.

Caicedo captaining Ecuador through pressure games matters. Enzo playing high-leverage minutes for Argentina matters.

Gusto and Hato absorbing tournament detail also helps Chelsea’s defensive reset.

But Chelsea cannot treat every tournament minute as clean preparation.

Alonso must decide who returns straight into tactical work, who needs a genuine pause and who can handle August without creating an avoidable injury bill by September.

That is where the James situation feels central.

If Chelsea’s captain carries a World Cup hamstring warning, the club’s right-sided structure becomes more than a selection debate.

It becomes an availability question that touches Gusto, the wider defensive rebuild and the need for control from midfield.

Read Chelsea has already looked at James’ captaincy test under Alonso, and the injury layer now makes that test sharper.

This is the hidden cost of a strong international footprint.

Chelsea want players good enough to survive deep into tournaments.

Alonso now has to make sure that status does not leave his first league weeks short of the very control those players are meant to provide.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United had a difficult evening once again as they were held to a 1-1 draw at Leeds United. Pressure mounts on Michael Carrick as United have just 7 points from 7 games.

Industry observers note that manchester United took the lead through Bryan Mbeumo in the first half, with the forward finishing Youri Tielemans’ excellent cross from the right. However, the visitors couldn’t hold on to their advantage as Dominic Calvert-Lewin equalised for Leeds United from a corner.

The draw extended United’s frustrating run of results, leaving Michael Carrick still searching for the consistency his side need.

Carragher, though, believes there were positives to take from the trip, particularly one performance at the back.

Jamie Carragher has singled out Harry Maguire for praise after Manchester United drew 1-1 with Leeds United at Elland Road on Sunday.

Speaking on Sky Sports, the former Liverpool defender admitted that picking up a point at Elland Road was not necessarily a bad result in isolation, even if United’s recent form made it feel like a missed opportunity.

“Going away to Leeds is going to be tricky for any team except for Manchester City and Arsenal at the moment,” Carragher remarked.

“A lot of teams will take a point at Leeds this season but the problem for Manchester United is the results have been so poor that they need to start winning games so it almost feels like two points dropped.”.

Carragher then turned his attention to Maguire, who he felt played a major role in keeping United in the game when Leeds began to push for a winner.

“But in isolation, getting a point at Leeds is a decent result. I thought Harry Maguire was fantastic, especially in the second half.”.

In a recent development, leeds United grew into the contest after Calvert-Lewin brought them level, putting United under pressure during the closing stages. Carragher felt Maguire’s efforts in defence helped prevent the visitors from falling apart.

“After Leeds got that goal back there was a stage of the game where it felt like Man United could go under, but Maguire at the back held it together for them. He was fantastic.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A fresh twist has emerged concerning the off-pitch drama at Millwall involving once highly-rated winger, Benicio Baker-Boaitey.

The Lions' start to the Championship season has been one of mixed fortunes, with Alex Neil's side sat 16th, having accumulated 18 points 15 matches.

Neil, one of the second tier's most seasoned managers, has been without several key names so far this season due to injury and suspension issues, which hasn't helped his side's wish for consistency.

One of the players missing in action for quite some time now is Baker-Boaitey, with it initially envisaged that the 22-year-old was also on the treatment table for a prolonged period.

However, recent developments have shed new light on the winger's situation, and it is one which could be about to get worse.

Baker-Boaitey arrived at Millwall in January 2025 after a spell with Premier League outfit, Brighton and Hove Albion, where he made six top-flight appearances for the Seagulls under Roberto De Zerbi after debuting against Chelsea in December 2023.

He would then link up with Port Vale for the 2024/25 League Two season, before his gametime in North Staffordshire was cut short due to injury, with Neil admitting after his move to SE16 was completed that Baker-Boaitey was suffering with pubic symphysis.

Almost two years later, though, the winger is yet to make a first-team appearance for the Lions, and was recently seen posting cryptic Instagram posts, one of which was captioned: "On my mumma, can't even train with the 21s.".

His account has since been deactivated, and it has since been widely reported that Millwall are now undertaking disciplinary action, which could even result in the termination of his contract, whilst Baker-Boaitey is also noted to be weighing up his options.

Given Brighton's recent ability for producing and unearthing several gems, there was an understandable hype when Millwall added Baker-Boaitey to their squad so soon after the club-record sale of Romain Esse - who has since returned to the club on loan - to Crystal Palace.

“Another England youth international, Benicio ticks a number of boxes we’re looking to recruit for at his young age of 21," mentioned Lions director of football, Steve Gallen.

"He is an exciting winger who will add plenty of pace and skill to the squad, which will get fans off their seats.".

However, this prediction has failed to come true, with Baker-Boaitey only making one appearance for the club's Under-21s side shortly after moving from the AMEX Stadium.

Millwall and West Ham United fans' disdain towards one another is certainly well-documented, and was displayed at The Den two months ago in a compelling 2-2 draw.

However, those from East London will certainly have one eye on how their rivals' disciplinary investigation into Baker-Boaitey's conduct plays out.

Indeed, the former England youth international came through the famous academy at Rush Green, and by 2020, aged 16, was linked with a move to Bayern Munich after rejecting professional terms at the London Stadium, eventually signing for FC Porto, with West Ham receiving £190,000 in compensation.

Industry observers note that millwall and West Ham fans, what do you make of the saga involving Benicio Baker-Boaitey? Comment below!

The German giants were not alone when it came to high-profile clubs courting his signature, with the likes of Liverpool, Paris Saint-Germain and Manchester United also credited with interest.

Since Baker-Boaitey's social media swipe, Neil is yet to issue a statement on the matter, and neither has the player.

Millwall will be hoping that this doesn't cause any form of distraction regardless of Baker-Boaitey's distinct lack of involvement since joining the club, whilst further impressions could be made on West Ham fans, even if returning to form under upcoming head coach, Scott Parker, is their top focus right now.

Industry observers note that malo Gusto’s World Cup has suddenly become more than a France subplot for Chelsea. It is now a live assessment of whether Xabi Alonso inherits a right-back worth protecting, reshaping or trading at the peak of his market.

Chelsea’s own interview with Gusto this week underlined the human part of that equation. The 23-year-old spoke about learning from N’Golo Kante, calling the former Blue one of the best midfielders France have produced and stressing the value of his example on and off the pitch.

Sources indicate that that matters because Kante is not just a nostalgic reference point. He remains the standard Chelsea supporters still use when judging humility, intensity and reliability in a high-pressure dressing room.

According to recent reports, for Gusto, those qualities arrive at a decisive moment. Reports around the player’s future claim Chelsea value him at around £75million, with the imminent Marco Palestra deal creating a more crowded full-back picture.

That number looks aggressive, but the logic is clear. Gusto is young, capped by France, under contract, Premier League-tested and capable of playing in several defensive structures.
